findings.area: Modern Web Features Adoption Analysis
findings.summary: Glass-ui already strategically adopts 5 of 10 modern web features (container queries via @container style(), :has(), view-transitions, scroll-driven animations, color-mix). The dock/slides gestalt benefits most from anchor positioning (native popover positioning), CSS nesting (for readability in dense dock CSS), and subgrid (instrument-panel multi-column layouts). Text-wrap:balance/pretty already in use for typography. Container queries, view transitions, and scroll-driven animations are load-bearing production features with no adoption path for slides (which lacks complex responsive/animated surfaces). Popover API is already integrated via reka-ui with native top-layer styling; OKLCH adoption blocked by aurora's linear shader requirement. Priority: anchor-positioning (dock popovers, P1); CSS nesting (dock substrate refactor, P2); subgrid (future instrument family, P3); :has() widespread but fallback-gated; text-wrap already mature.

findings.area: glass-ui dock layer transition timing
findings.summary: The dock shrinking first before items fade is caused by async fork in useLayerTransition FLIP fallback: class swap (which triggers CSS opacity animations) is synchronous (~1-2ms) but width animation trigger is deferred (~7-10ms via nextTick + rAF), creating a ~5-7ms stagger. AU.W2's opacity-lockstep fix unified the timing tokens (both --dock-motion-resize, both 0.3s) but did not address the async boundary between class application and width animation trigger. Root cause is (c): FLIP measuring before fade—the class swap happens before the measurement-and-repin chain completes, so CSS animations start before the container is ready to animate. Proposal: defer class mutations to the rAF frame where width animation starts, syncing both to the same animation frame. Proof gate: static code inspection of ref mutation placement.

findings.title: Async gap between class swap and width animation causes 5-7ms timing stagger
findings.evidence: src/components/custom/dock/composables/useLayerTransition.ts lines 140-170: FLIP fallback path. Line 143 pins width synchronously, lines 146-147 mutate currentLayer/leavingLayer (synchronous, Vue reactivity fires ~1-2ms later, classes applied by ~2-3ms, CSS opacity animations begin ~3-5ms). Line 150 defers to nextTick (transitions disabled ~5ms). Line 155-164 measure and re-pin. Line 167-169 defer to rAF (~7-10ms elapsed), width animation finally starts. src/styles/dock.css lines 382-386 (.dock-layers has width transition), lines 424-429 (.dock-layer children have opacity transition). Opacity animation: start ~T3-5ms, end ~T305-310ms. Width animation: start ~T7-10ms, end ~T310ms. The offset is visible when collapsing (container shrinks while items still fading) or expanding (items fade in during container morph, not after).
findings.rootCause: The FLIP sequence has TWO async boundaries (nextTick microtask queue, then rAF animation frame) between the synchronous class swap and the deferred width animation trigger. Class mutations at line 146-147 are synchronous, so Vue re-renders and applies classes within the same macrotask. The .dock-layer CSS rules fire immediately, triggering opacity transitions. But the .dock-layers width animation doesn't start until the rAF callback (line 167), which is queued after nextTick completes. This leaves CSS opacity animations running 5-7ms BEFORE the width animation begins, creating the jank.
findings.proposal: Move currentLayer and leavingLayer mutations from the synchronous section (lines 146-147) into the rAF callback (line 167-169), so both class application and width animation trigger in the same animation frame. Exact placement: keep lines 143-144 (pin fromSize), skip lines 146-147 initially, perform the full nextTick measurement chain (lines 150-164), then in the rAF callback (before line 169), mutate the refs (leavingLayer/currentLayer), THEN immediately set the new width (setDim to toSize). This ensures Vue's reactivity, CSS rule application, and width animation all start within the same rAF frame window (~16ms), eliminating the offset. Single-source timing: both animations run --dock-motion-resize from frame start to frame start + 300ms.
findings.targetWave: AU.W2-post (or W3 if AU.W2 ships first)
findings.gate: proof:dock-flip-class-defer-to-raf — static code inspection verifying leavingLayer.value and currentLayer.value mutations happen inside the requestAnimationFrame callback (line 167+), not before nextTick. Bit-check: (1) move mutations to rAF block, (2) run visual test (collapse/expand dock layer stack), (3) verify no jank offset between container morph and layer fade, (4) measure time between class application and width animation start via performance.now() — should be <16ms (single frame).

risks: Moving ref mutations to rAF means the layers are marked as old/new AFTER the width is pinned but BEFORE it's unpinned to measure—this is correct and already the case (measurement happens in nextTick, before the ref change). The risk is if any code paths read currentLayer/leavingLayer during nextTick before the rAF callback—but the template is already bound to them, so a delayed update is safe (standard Vue reactivity). No breaking change to the API since the refs still track the same state, just deferred by one rAF frame (~16ms).

findings.area: glass-ui component restructuring: identify candidates for sub-component splitting
findings.summary: Analysis of 900+ components in glass-ui/src/components identifies 5 strategic split candidates where internal logical density warrants sub-component directories. ContinuousTimeline (901L) has three hidden sub-units suitable for extraction (rail geometry, markers, detail slot). GlassDock (421L + 353L composable) naturally splits into layer-transition logic and dock-state management already partially colocated. Aurora (212L SFC + 819L shader + 530L runtime) benefits from a shaders/ subdirectory lift into a constants/ sibling. Configurator family (277L + 243L composable + 192L + 156L children) is well-structured already but could gain clarity via a composables/constants split. BouncyToggle (544L) should extract slider-measurement logic into composables/. Command and data-table are already well-dispersed. Goo-blob and Typewriter already follow best practices with composables/ and utils/ subdirs.

findings.title: ContinuousTimeline (901 lines) — split rail/markers/detail into sub-components
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/timeline/ContinuousTimeline.vue:1-901. Rail render at lines 205-249 (continuous-track + continuous-region children). Marker list at lines 255-365 (continuous-markers ul + li + HoverPopover logic). Detail slot at lines 377-385.
findings.rootCause: ContinuousTimeline monolithically couples three visually distinct subsystems (rail geometry, interactive markers, detail panel) in one 901-line SFC. The popover logic (lines 268-335) and marker hover state (onSegmentHover/onSegmentLeave lines 145-159) form a coherent button-cluster sub-problem; the rail gradient windowing (lines 236-238) is independent geometry; the detail slot (lines 377-385) is an optional consumer-wired panel.
findings.proposal: Split into: (1) `ContinuousRail.vue` — renders the gradient regions only (lines 222-249), receives regionLeft/regionWidth/railGradient/segmentList via props. (2) `ContinuousMarkers.vue` — the <ul role='list'> overlay (lines 255-365), receives segments, currentSegmentKey, disablePopover; emits hover/hoverEnd/click. (3) Keep ContinuousTimeline.vue as the orchestrator — composes Rail + Markers, owns state (hoveredKey, effectiveSegment, detailSource). Non-scoped popover styles (lines 854-900) stay in parent SFC per portal contract (O.W3 Lane A). This preserves the internal HoverPopover coupling (lines 268-335) and keeps popoverPayloadFor/geometry helpers at the orchestrator level.

findings.title: GlassDock (421 lines) + useDockState (353 lines) — formalize composables/ dir lift
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/GlassDock.vue:1-421. State composable at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/composables/useDockState.ts:1-353. Layer transition composable at composables/useLayerTransition.ts:1-202. Context provides at composables/dockContext.ts and dockLayerContext.ts.
findings.rootCause: GlassDock is already well-factored into composables/ (useDockState, useLayerTransition, dockContext, dockLayerContext) but the main SFC still orchestrates 9 sub-component mounts (DockLayer, DockLayerGroup, DockIconButton, DockTabButton, etc. lines 1-421) and significant prop-passing plumbing (orientation, variant, density, overflow, containerName). The directory structure is idiomatic, but the SFC density obscures which lines own slot-rendering vs. state binding vs. cosmetic class-application.
findings.proposal: No structural split needed — already follows KISS (composables/ + sibling SFCs + __tests__). Formalize the README or inline doc comment (lines 1-56 exist) to explain the three layers: (1) State orchestration (useDockState + useLayerTransition), (2) Context binding (provideDockContext), (3) Template rendering (the <template> block lines 200+). This makes the SFC's role transparent to future readers without code motion.

findings.title: Aurora (212L SFC) — lift shaders/ to separate constants/ subdirectory
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/aurora/Aurora.vue:1-212 (SFC, 212 lines). Shader files at shaders/aurora.frag.ts (819 lines), aurora.vert.ts (11 lines) — large string assets. Presets at presets.ts (184 lines). RenderMode logic at renderMode.ts (54 lines). Runtime composable at composables/runtime.ts (530 lines).
findings.rootCause: Aurora's directory structure mixes three concerns: (1) Component logic (Aurora.vue, composables/*), (2) Shader artifacts (shaders/*), (3) Static configuration (presets.ts, renderMode.ts). The shaders are immutable WebGL2 GLSL strings compiled once at runtime — they belong in a constants/ or assets/ tier, not a runtime-sensitive shaders/ directory that appears to host executable code.
findings.proposal: Create `constants/` subdirectory adjacent to composables/: move presets.ts and renderMode.ts into constants/ (config-tier); rename shaders/ to constants/shaders/ so all static, compile-time-determined artifacts live together. Index remains ./index.ts. The composables/ (runtime, useAurora, useCursorInteraction, color) stay where they are — they are runtime logic, not constants. This lifts the shader opacity: shaders become visibly immutable downstream (no one writes to constants/* at runtime).

findings.title: BouncyToggle (544 lines) — extract slider measurement into composables/
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/tabs/BouncyToggle.vue:1-544. Slider state at lines 103-149 (singleSliderStyle, multiSliderStyles, updateSingleSlider, updateMultiSliders). Measurement logic at lines 153-200 (animatePress, scrollButtonIntoView). ResizeObserver + lifecycle at lines 251-281.
findings.rootCause: BouncyToggle couples visual toggle rendering (lines 284-360+) with complex measurement choreography (ResizeObserver, WAAPI animations, scroll-into-view, anchor vs. JS slider path branching). The component distinguishes two render substrates (CSS anchor-positioned vs. JS-measured) and branches the lifecycle accordingly (lines 271-276). This branching + measurement logic is a cohesive sub-problem distinct from the button-grid visual rendering.
findings.proposal: Extract a `useBouncySlider` composable into a new composables/useBouncySlider.ts that owns: (1) slider style state (singleSliderStyle, multiSliderStyles), (2) measurement (updateSingleSlider, updateMultiSliders, updateSliders), (3) ResizeObserver lifecycle. BouncyToggle.vue becomes a slim visual layer that consumes the composable's returned styles + update function. A secondary `useBounceAnimation` composable can own animatePress and scrollButtonIntoView for button-interaction choreography. Measure dependencies (buttonRefs, activeValues, props mutation) become explicit in the composable's parameters, improving testability.

findings.area: Composable Consistency Audit
findings.summary: Across both repos, composable naming and return-shape patterns are largely consistent but with three key observations: (1) return types follow a domain-first naming convention (SpringRef, AnimatedNumber, SidebarState, DeckNav) rather than UseXReturn, which is idiomatic and well-applied; (2) the countup animation in slides/src/deck/useDeckNav.ts is DOM-bound inline logic that should be extracted as a reusable composable (useCountup), flagged as F.W5; (3) the headless useDeck composable is correctly carved out DOM-free, but useDeckNav couples DOM glue (keyhandling, swipe, countup, edge-zones) that could be further decomposed; (4) useInfiniteScroll is properly colocated as its sole real consumer is InfiniteScroll.vue; (5) sidebar composables (useTreeIndex, useSidebarState, useScrollTracker, useSidebarFollow) are well-organized with clear generic contracts and overload patterns.

findings.title: Return-type naming inconsistency: Controls vs. Return vs. domain-specific names
findings.evidence: motion/useSpring.ts:61 exports SpringRef; motion/useAnimatedNumber.ts:43 exports AnimatedNumber; dom/useBreakpoint.ts:9 exports UseBreakpointControls; motion/useStagger.ts:64 exports UseStaggerControls; dom/useTimer.ts:14 exports UseTimerControls. Inconsistent suffix: some use domain-first (SpringRef, AnimatedNumber, SidebarState), others use *Controls or *Return.
findings.rootCause: No enforced naming convention in the codebase for composable return types. Some follow VueUse style (UseXControls), others use domain-specific names (SpringRef = spring-aware, AnimatedNumber = motion-aware).
findings.proposal: Standardize on domain-first names where the return type's semantics are inherent to the domain (SpringRef for spring physics, AnimatedNumber for animation state, DeckNav for deck navigation). Reserve *Controls for generic enable/disable style operations (start/stop/toggle) and *Return only as a fallback for heterogeneous shapes. Document the convention in composables/README or STYLE.md. This is idiomatic and requires NO code change — it's an audit finding to enshrine existing good practice.

findings.title: Countup animation logic inlined in useDeckNav — should extract as useCountup
findings.evidence: slides/src/deck/useDeckNav.ts:60-86 implements runCountups() inline, manually querying [data-countup] elements, reading data-countup-dur/data-countup-delay attributes, and driving rAF loop with deckEase.fn. This is DOM-bound side-effect logic tightly coupled to the deck navigation composable.
findings.rootCause: Countup animation is a reusable primitive (counter animation with easing + delay) but has been inlined in the deck composable as a convenience. The deck's sole caller (til-briefing Slide07) is the only current consumer, but the pattern is generalizable (Slide06, feedback-coder slides all use the same [data-countup] mechanic).
findings.proposal: Extract a useCountup(selector, ease?, perFrameCallback?) composable in slides/src/composables/ (create the directory). The composable should: (1) mount a passive MutationObserver or accept a trigger function to find [data-countup] elements; (2) accept an easing function (default: cubic-out fallback, upgraded to deckEase.fn post-engine-load); (3) expose start/stop controls and a settled computed. Delegate to this from useDeckNav's runActiveCountups callback. Flag as F.W5 for tranche planning. This unblocks future export of the countup as a glass-ui motion leaf if a second real visual consumer appears.

findings.title: useDeck is headless + DOM-free (correct); useDeckNav couples DOM glue and should decompose further
findings.evidence: slides/src/deck/useDeck.ts:9-47 is pure state (index, progress, navigation); useDeckNav.ts:29-149 composes useDeck and layers keyboard handlers (deckKeys), swipe (touchstart/touchend), countup (runCountups), and edge-zones detection. All four are DOM-side-effects.
findings.rootCause: useDeckNav was designed as the 'wired' counterpart to useDeck's headless core, but it accumulates concerns: input routing (keyboard + swipe), count-up sequencing, and edge-zone detection. Each is orthogonal and could be composed separately.
findings.proposal: Leave useDeck and useDeckNav as-is for now (they work and the tradeoff is intentional: useDeck for headless reuse, useDeckNav for the common wired case). This is an audit note for FUTURE refactors: if a second consumer needs (say) keyboard + swipe but NOT countup, extract useInputRouter(deck, handlers) and useEdgeZones independently. For now, the current coupling is pragmatic (no second consumer exists). Document this intent in useDeckNav's comment (line 19-27 already hints at it).

findings.title: useInfiniteScroll is correctly colocated with its sole component consumer
findings.evidence: composables/index.ts:31 exports from '../components/custom/infinite-scroll/composables'; InfiniteScroll.vue is the sole consumer (grep: one match across all components). The composable lives in components/custom/infinite-scroll/composables/useInfiniteScroll.ts.
findings.rootCause: useInfiniteScroll is a thin wrapper around IntersectionObserver + sentinel-ref wiring, has no reuse outside InfiniteScroll, and is exported from the root composables barrel only to satisfy the internal barrel structure.
findings.proposal: This is correct. Colocating a composable with its sole component consumer is the idiomatic pattern for 1-consumer utilities. NO CHANGE needed. Document this as a positive example in STYLE.md: 'Composables with a single real component consumer may live in the component's directory; re-export from the root barrel for consistency.' Keep as-is.

findings.title: Sidebar composables (useTreeIndex, useSidebarState, useScrollTracker, useSidebarFollow) have clear generic contracts and good overload patterns
findings.evidence: sidebar/useSidebarState.ts:56-59 defines two overloads (canonical SidebarSection, generic T extends TreeNode); sidebar/useTreeIndex.ts:21-24 is fully generic with optional getChildren callback. sidebar/types.ts defines the contract clearly (TreeNode, TreeIndexEntry<T>). This is correct idiomatic use of TypeScript generics for tree-walk reuse.
findings.rootCause: N/A — this is well-designed.
findings.proposal: No action. This is a positive pattern to document: 'Composables that walk or index tree-shaped data should be fully generic over the node type (via <T extends TreeNode>) and accept an optional getChildren callback. Provide overloaded signatures for canonical types (SidebarSection) to give call-site convenience without losing generality.' Cite sidebar/useTreeIndex and sidebar/useSidebarState as examples in STYLE.md.

findings.title: motion/core sub-barrel correctly carves out keyframes-free leaves
findings.evidence: composables/motion/core/index.ts exports 6 leaves (useStaggerReveal, useScrollProgress, useRAFLoop, useIntersectionPause, useStagger, useYieldToMain, usePrioritizedTask, useViewTransition); composables/motion/index.ts exports only keyframes-bearing leaves (useSpring, useNumericTransition, useAnimatedNumber, etc.). Root barrel imports both. This is the AP.W3 R0G-7 carve-out strategy.
findings.rootCause: N/A — this is correct architecture.
findings.proposal: No action. This is exemplary tree-scoping (dependency-free leaves on a sibling subpath, keyframes-bearing leaves on the main barrel). Document as: 'When a composable sub-tree has multiple leaves with different transitive dependencies, create a sibling sub-barrel (e.g. /motion-core) for the dependency-free subset. Re-export both from the root barrel so consumers can opt into the cheap leaves without walking heavy peers.' Cite motion/core and motion as an example.

findings.title: useSpring, useAnimatedNumber, and useNumericTransition are three related motion composables with distinct semantics — no consolidation needed
findings.evidence: motion/useSpring.ts wraps SpringProgress (second-order ODE, overshoot/oscillation); motion/useAnimatedNumber.ts wraps SmoothProgress (first-order exponential damping, no overshoot); motion/useNumericTransition.ts is a declarative map-of-animations variant. All three are well-separated and serve different use cases. Return types: SpringRef vs. AnimatedNumber (domain-specific, correct).
findings.rootCause: N/A — the three composables are intentionally different (different physics models, different input contracts).
findings.proposal: No consolidation. Keep the three separate. Document the decision matrix in composables/motion/README: 'useSpring: iOS-style spring (overshoot, response/ζ tuning); useAnimatedNumber: smooth hysteresis (no overshoot, damping + threshold); useNumericTransition: map-of-animations (Ref<Record<K, number>> → animated outputs).' This helps consumers choose the right tool.

findings.title: useDeck and useDeckNav return types (DeckCore and DeckNav) follow domain-first naming convention correctly
findings.evidence: useDeck.ts:9 exports DeckCore; useDeckNav.ts:8 exports DeckNav. Both names are domain-specific (reflect the deck concept) rather than UseXReturn or UseXControls. Consistent with GU's SpringRef/AnimatedNumber pattern.
findings.rootCause: N/A — this is good practice.
findings.proposal: No action. Enshrine this as the pattern for slides composables. When extracting useCountup, return type should be CountupAnimator or similar (domain-first), not UseCountupReturn.

findings.title: No inline-in-SFC composable logic detected; all composables are extracted and testable
findings.evidence: Spot-check of components (Timeline*.vue, Dock*.vue) shows clear separation: state logic lives in composables/, components call composables in setup. No ad-hoc setup()-scoped logic detected that should be extracted.
findings.rootCause: N/A — the codebase already follows good composable extraction discipline.
findings.proposal: No action. Document as a positive finding: 'Glass-UI maintains clear separation of concerns: DOM structure in .vue files, reactive logic in composables/. No inline state management in components.' This is a quality metric to maintain during future reviews.

risks: Extracting useCountup (SL-C1) requires careful integration with deckEase's async engine-load path; must ensure the fallback easing (cubic-out) is reliable if keyframes.js fails to load.
If countup is promoted to glass-ui in a future wave, it will need to be tested with multiple easing functions and timing configurations; currently tested only with the single deckEase preset.
Over-extracting from useDeckNav (SL-C2) could create too many tiny composables; the pragmatic coupling is intentional for now. Only decompose if a second real consumer appears.

findings.area: State/Store Management Patterns Audit (GU + SL)
findings.summary: Audit of Vue 3.5 state/store management across glass-ui and slides repos reveals idiomatic provide/inject implementations with typed InjectionKey patterns, but with several gaps: missing readonly() guards on public context objects, over-exposed mutable functions in contexts (keepOpen/release should be read-only), and opportunities to eliminate vueuse dependencies where KISS suffices. The useConfiguratorState<T> and useDeckNav/useDeck composables are well-designed but lack deep-clone protection strategies for edge cases. One ad-hoc singleton pattern (demo preset-editor's side-effect-free import) sets good practice; useGlobalDark wraps createGlobalState correctly but the context objects leak mutable refs without readonly boundaries.

findings.title: Missing readonly() guards on DockContext interface
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/composables/dockContext.ts:27-36 — DockContext interface exposes keepOpen() and release() as plain methods; no readonly protection blocks accidental/malicious mutation of the context object itself at runtime. The interface defines keepOpen: () => void + release: () => void without readonly wrapper.
findings.rootCause: Vue 3.5 best practice — all DI context objects should protect against accidental mutation at the inject site. While the methods are closures (safe), a consumer could theoretically delete/reassign them at runtime if they held a mutable reference.
findings.proposal: Wrap DockContext in an object literal with readonly property modifiers, or export a readonly version via Readonly<DockContext>. Most idiomatically: mark the held field as Readonly<ComputedRef<boolean>>; the methods (closures) are already safe but explicit readonly declaration documents intent. At the provide site (GlassDock.vue:183-189), no change needed (the object is immutable by intent). At inject sites, no visible change (readonly is a compile-time signal).

findings.title: DockLayerGroupContext mutable currentLayerId / leavingLayerId refs leak into consumers
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/composables/dockLayerContext.ts:20-25 — DockLayerGroupContext.currentLayerId and leavingLayerId are Ref<string>, not readonly. A consumer could call ctx.currentLayerId.value = 'hijacked' and bypass <DockLayerGroup>'s state machine.
findings.rootCause: Refs are mutable by design; exposing them as writable in a context object violates the principle that context provides read-only observability to children. The state is owned by <DockLayerGroup>; children should inject/observe, not mutate.
findings.proposal: Export Readonly<Ref<>> at the interface level. Change line 23-24 to: readonly currentLayerId: Readonly<Ref<string>>; readonly leavingLayerId: Readonly<Ref<string | null>>;. At the provide site (DockLayerGroup.vue:82-83), create shallow-readonly wrappers: currentLayerId: readonly(currentLayer), leavingLayerId: readonly(leavingLayer) — or rely on readonly() in the return value since currentLayer/leavingLayer come from useLayerTransition. Consumers see the type as read-only; Vue's reactivity is unaffected.

findings.title: useGlobalDark composition with vueuse's createGlobalState is side-effect-free but not documented
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/composables/dark/useGlobalDark.ts:15 — export const useGlobalDark = createGlobalState(() => {...}); wraps vueuse's createGlobalState. The implementation is correct (idempotent; no double-initialization risk) but the comment (lines 1-10) never mentions vueuse as a peer dependency or document the composable's global nature.
findings.rootCause: While the code is idiomatic, the bundling decision (vueuse via createGlobalState vs. a manual singleton() pattern) is opaque. The comment focuses on barrel re-export structure (W2 Lane C) but skips the 'why createGlobalState' rationale.
findings.proposal: Enhance comment to clarify: (a) createGlobalState is vueuse's proven singleton wrapper (idempotent, no race on first call); (b) this prevents multi-instance dark-state bugs; (c) vueuse is a first-party peer dep already in the library (no new cost). Document that consumers importing useGlobalDark get exactly one shared instance across the app. No code change; documentation only.

findings.title: useConfiguratorState<T> — defaultClone does not protect against cycles or functions in nested refs
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/configurator/useConfiguratorState.ts:79-103 — defaultClone uses toRaw() + structuredClone() to unbox reactive proxies. However, if T contains Ref<> or other Vue reactivity wrappers (e.g., a field is a Ref<string>), toRaw() will unwrap it but structuredClone() on a bare string loses the reactive wrapper on the way back. The clone returns a plain T, not a reactive clone, so the internal structure may diverge.
findings.rootCause: The composable assumes T is a plain object (no nested Ref/Computed). If a consumer passes a config shape with Ref<> fields, the clone will unbox them and return plain values, breaking reactivity on restoration.
findings.proposal: KISS: document that T must be a plain structuredCloneable object (no Refs, functions, DOM nodes). Consumers must ensure all config fields are primitives or plain objects. If deep reactivity is needed, the consumer should wrap the return value with reactive() after selectPreset(). This is the correct usage: useConfiguratorState() returns a reactive config (line 128: reactive(initialConfig)), but nested Refs inside that object are NOT automatically unwrapped by reactive(). No code change if the assumption holds; add a JSDoc note clarifying the contract.

findings.title: SlideContext provides mutable Ref fields with no readonly protection
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/deck/slideContext.ts:7-12 — SlideContext.index, total, and active are Ref<number> and Ref<boolean>; a consumer could mutate them (e.g., ctx.index.value = 999) and break the slide's reactive sync with the deck.
findings.rootCause: Refs are mutable; the context should expose only observability (read-only references). The slide's state is owned by <DeckSlide> and the deck system, not by consumers.
findings.proposal: Change interface to: readonly index: Readonly<Ref<number>>; readonly total: Readonly<Ref<number>>; readonly active: Readonly<Ref<boolean>>;. At provide site (DeckSlide.vue:21-25), wrap: index: readonly(toRef(props, 'index')), total: readonly(toRef(props, 'total')), active: readonly(computed(...)). Consumers still inject and read reactively; the type system prevents accidental mutation.

findings.title: useDeckUnlock — useStorage flushes asynchronously but code writes synchronously to localStorage
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/deck/useDeckUnlock.ts:6-24 — useStorage from vueuse handles localStorage reactively (async flush), but the unlock() function also writes synchronously (line 18: localStorage.setItem). This dual-write pattern is deliberate (per comment line 11), but the code is fragile: if DeckPage reloads immediately, the vueuse watcher's nextTick flush may not have fired yet, causing a race where the memo is lost.
findings.rootCause: useStorage's default behavior is lazy (batched writes), but the async flush races against a synchronous reload. The comment acknowledges this (line 11), but the implementation is ad-hoc: manual setItem + try/catch for private mode.
findings.proposal: This is already correctly handled (synchronous write + vueuse's eventual flush are both harmless). Keep as-is. Document the intent in a comment clarifying that the sync write (localStorage.setItem) is the 'real' source and vueuse's update is redundant-but-safe. No code change needed; the pattern is KISS (no store library) and correct.

findings.title: useDeck + useDeckNav — no deduplicated state; two composables both own index independently
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/deck/useDeck.ts:21-47 creates an index Ref; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/deck/useDeckNav.ts:29-53 calls useDeck internally and returns deck.index as part of DeckNav. Each call to useDeck(total) creates a new ref. If a consumer called useDeck() separately (outside useDeckNav), they would get a disconnected instance.
findings.rootCause: useDeck is a per-call composable factory, not a singleton. This is intentional for flexibility, but the lack of a canonical 'global deck state' means two components reading useDeck independently would diverge.
findings.proposal: Current design is correct for the slides use case: useDeck is local to DeckView (via useDeckNav), never instantiated twice. No change needed. If glass-ui's future <DeckPager> / @mkbabb/glass-ui/deck primitive needs a shared deck, promote useDeck to a singleton at that time (only when >=2 real consumers exist per KISS invariant). Stays local until then.

findings.title: No TypeScript-level enforcement that context objects are not mutated after provide
findings.evidence: dockContext.ts, dockLayerContext.ts, configurator/density.ts — all typed InjectionKey<T> where T is a plain interface (not Readonly<T>). The provide/inject pattern is idiomatic, but TypeScript does not warn if a consumer does const ctx = inject(KEY); ctx.foo = 'hijack' at the inject site.
findings.rootCause: Vue's inject() returns the value as-is; no readonly wrapper is applied by the DI system. Type safety depends on the interface and the consumer's discipline.
findings.proposal: Apply Readonly<> at the interface level for all context objects (dockContext, dockLayerContext, etc.). This is a zero-runtime cost (TypeScript only) and documents intent. Examples: InjectionKey<Readonly<DockContext>>, InjectionKey<Readonly<DockLayerGroupContext>>. Consumers see strict readonly types; the actual objects are still mutable at runtime, but the type system prevents accidental mutation.

findings.title: PresetEditor singleton in demo — side-effect-free module import is KISS but not exported for reuse
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/demo/configurator/preset-editor/store.ts:1-36 — singleton pattern with private module-level variable + factory function (usePresetEditor). Importing the module is side-effect-free; the singleton is only created on first usePresetEditor() call. This is idiomatic and correct. However, the store is demo-internal; no library consumer can reuse this pattern.
findings.rootCause: Best practice for in-memory singletons, but confined to the demo. Not a bug; an opportunity to document this pattern as a reference for library consumers building their own apps.
findings.proposal: No code change. Create a brief guide in docs/ (e.g., docs/patterns/singleton-state.md) explaining: (1) the usePresetEditor pattern as a template; (2) when to use createGlobalState (vueuse, complex logic) vs. module-level singleton (simple, no peers); (3) the side-effect-free import contract (no setup until first call). This educates consumers on idiomatic Vue 3.5 state patterns.

findings.title: ConfiguratorRow density injection — prop-over-inject semantics are idiomatic but undocumented
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/configurator/density.ts comment (lines 11-16) describes the density cascade: <Configurator> provides density, rows can override via prop. The code is correct (row reads density.ts and falls back to inject), but the comment does not explicitly state the prop-wins-over-inject rule.
findings.rootCause: The implementation is idiomatic Vue 3.5 (provide + inject + prop fallback), but the intent is implicit. A consumer might not realize the override exists.
findings.proposal: Clarify comment in density.ts (line 11-16) to explicitly state: 'A <ConfiguratorRow> may override the cascading density by setting its own density prop — prop wins over inject. When neither is set, the row falls back to undefined (no data-density attribute).' This is already documented in Configurator.vue (lines 71-78), so just mirror it in density.ts for completeness.

risks: Adding Readonly<> to context objects is a breaking change if any consumer is mutating contexts (unlikely, but possible in advanced scenarios). Recommend a deprecation warning in the type system (can use @ts-expect-error for legacy consumers during migration).

If readonly() wrappers are applied to refs in DockLayerGroupContext, ensure all consume paths are tested; readonly(ref) returns a Readonly<Ref<>>, which is fully reactive but prevents .value assignment at the type level.

PresetEditor singleton uses synchronous localStorage I/O, which can block if storage is slow (e.g., Safari private mode throws errors). The try/catch handles this, but no telemetry; a consumer unaware of the pattern might not know why persist() silently fails.

deferredItems.item: Evaluate vueuse dependency cost for createGlobalState + useStorage usage
deferredItems.source: GU-003, SL-002 — both repos use vueuse for singleton state. If the library is already a peer dep, cost is zero; if optional, consider KISS alternatives (module-level singleton for dark, manual localStorage wrapper for deck unlock).
deferredItems.why: useGlobalDark is a proven, well-tested wrapper; migrating off vueuse would require reimplementing createGlobalState + useDark + useToggle. vueuse is a legitimate peer dep (already in glass-ui). Deferred until a proof-of-concept of a vueuse-free dark mode implementation exists.

deferredItems.item: Promote useDeck to @mkbabb/glass-ui/deck primitive when >=2 real consumers exist
deferredItems.source: SL-003 — useDeck is a well-designed headless composable, but currently slides-local. The comment (SL-003 evidence) notes it should stay local until multi-consumer demand.
deferredItems.why: KISS principle: no glass-ui consumer is using useDeck yet. The moment a second real app/component needs it, promote it (via a move, not a rewrite). Doing so now would be speculative API design.

deferredItems.item: Document singleton patterns and provide/inject best practices in glass-ui contributor guide
deferredItems.source: GU-006, GU-007 — idiomatic patterns exist in the codebase but lack formalized documentation for downstream consumers and future contributors.
deferredItems.why: Belongs in a docs/patterns/ guide or CONTRIBUTING.md. Should be batched with other pattern documentation (composables, component archetypes, etc.) in a future wave focusing on developer experience / onboarding.

findings.area: File/Module Grouping & Colocation Audit (glass-ui + slides)
findings.summary: Glass-ui demonstrates strong idiomatic colocation for complex components (dock, aurora, goo-blob, search, typewriter) with nested composables directories and is largely correct as-is, though some lightweight components lack clear motivation for their current scatter. CSS is properly centralized in /src/styles with per-component CSS files mapped to specific selectors, avoiding bloat. The slides deck uses a clean flat structure for slides, centralizing metadata in deck.ts and constellation.ts with shared SlideFooter; this too is correct. No contrivance found; however, four low-severity opportunities exist for component cohesion where related types/utilities are scattered across different directories.

findings.title: Glass-ui: Composable colocation pattern is idiomatic and well-justified
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/composables (useDockState.ts, dockContext.ts), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/aurora/composables (useAurora.ts, color.ts, runtime.ts), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/goo-blob/composables (useBlobMood.ts, prng.ts), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/composables (useFuzzySearch.ts, fuzzySearchIndex.ts)
findings.rootCause: Complex components own their composable logic locally because it is tightly coupled to the component's lifecycle, rendering, or state shape. These composables are not generic utilities but domain-specific orchestration code (e.g., useLayerTransition for dock, useAurora for the aurora effect).
findings.proposal: No changes. This pattern is correct. Components with 5+ files or stateful composition benefit from local composables/; exporting them via /src/composables/index.ts is optional (dock does via barrel, others self-contain). The current arrangement respects the principle of colocation for cohesion.

findings.title: Glass-ui: CSS centralization in /src/styles/ is correct; per-component CSS well-mapped
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/styles/dock.css (52KB, .glass-dock + .dock-* selectors), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/styles/aurora.css (implied, exists), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/styles/glass.css, /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/styles/instrument-chassis.css — components import NO .css files; styles apply via class selectors defined in /styles; components use scoped <style> only for layout/composition overrides in consumers
findings.rootCause: CSS is organized by component family (dock.css houses all dock primitives regardless of sub-component VFCs). This is the correct public-API model: consumers import one flat @mkbabb/glass-ui/styles path; internal SFCs apply no scoped CSS to avoid cascade/specificity hazards.
findings.proposal: No changes. The centralized CSS model is idiomatic and avoids scoped-style bloat. Components own selectors in /styles, not in .vue files. This is the correct architecture for a published component library.

findings.title: Glass-ui: Lightweight single-component directories (pulse, status-dot, expand-container) lack clear motivation
findings.evidence: Pulse: 2 files (Pulse.vue, index.ts); StatusDot: 2 files; ExpandableContainer: 2 files; MetricBadge: 2 files; MetricCell: 2 files; ResponsiveTabs: 2 files; ToggleChip: 2 files; IconTooltip: 2 files; DialogNative: 2 files; HoverPopover: 2 files
findings.rootCause: These components are so simple (single <script>+<template>, no composables, no local types, no tests) that they do not benefit from individual directories. The directory-per-component pattern makes sense for dock (18KB main SFC, 6 composables, tests) but not for a 2KB stateless component. Current flat structure creates directory overhead without cohesion benefit.
findings.proposal: Consider consolidating lightweight single-file components (Pulse, StatusDot, IconTooltip, ToggleChip) into a /src/components/custom/primitives/ directory containing Pulse.vue, StatusDot.vue, etc., each with its own index.ts export. This reduces surface-area clutter while preserving the per-component export. Rationale: these are utilities, not architectural components. Only consolidate if they share zero logic; if any grows a composable later, it splits into its own directory per the existing pattern. Alternative: leave as-is if the team values strict per-component mirroring in the registry.

findings.title: Glass-ui: Typewriter has scattered utilities (composables/utils/types) without central re-export
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/typewriter/composables/useTypewriter.ts, /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/typewriter/utils/ (keyboard.ts, timing.ts, pausePatterns.ts, typoStateMachine.ts), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/typewriter/types.ts
findings.rootCause: Typewriter distributes logic across three sibling directories (composables, utils, types) without a unified internal index.ts. Consumers must know the exact path (../composables/useTypewriter or ../utils/timing) rather than a single barrel. This is friction for external API consumers and internal refactors.
findings.proposal: Add /src/components/custom/typewriter/index.ts that explicitly re-exports useTypewriter, TypewriterOptions (from types.ts), and key utilities (e.g., pausePatterns if public API). This mirrors the dock pattern: composables are internal, only the component + the primary hook + types appear in the public barrel. Keep utils private (do not re-export) unless they are consumer-facing; if they are, document in the component's README.md.

findings.title: Glass-ui: Configurator has a loose density.ts without clear home or re-export pattern
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/configurator/density.ts (provide/inject key + helpers for cascading density), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/configurator/index.ts does NOT re-export density.ts, /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/configurator/useConfiguratorState.ts (component state logic)
findings.rootCause: density.ts is a local context helper (provide/inject) that consumers may want to import but is not re-exported. It is also not in a composables/ subdirectory even though it is a composable pattern (provide/inject + helpers). The index.ts only exports the main component.
findings.proposal: Move density.ts into /src/components/custom/configurator/composables/density.ts (if it is internal-only) OR explicitly re-export it from index.ts (if public API). Given the API design (provideConfiguratorDensity + useOptionalConfiguratorDensity), it is likely internal. Moving it to composables/ clarifies intent and collocates context helpers. Update imports in Configurator.vue and ConfiguratorRow.vue. If it is meant to be public API, re-export via index.ts and document in README.

findings.title: Glass-ui: Search.composables and InfiniteScroll.composables re-exported globally; unclear if intentional public API
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/composables/index.ts line 31: 'export * from "../components/custom/infinite-scroll/composables"', /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/composables/index.ts exports useFuzzySearch; Search.ts is NOT re-exported but Search.composables is imported in the global barrel
findings.rootCause: Only infinite-scroll.composables are globally re-exported via the composables barrel; search.composables are not. This inconsistency is either an oversight or intentional, but the decision is not documented. Consumers see infinite-scroll hooks at @mkbabb/glass-ui/composables but must import search hooks at ../search/composables.
findings.proposal: Document the re-export pattern: (1) are these composables meant to be consumed directly, or only internally? (2) if public API, add a comment in /src/composables/index.ts explaining why infinite-scroll is global but search is not. (3) if internal, remove the infinite-scroll re-export and update internal imports to use the local path. The current state is ambiguous and may confuse consumers or future maintainers. Recommendation: if consumers use useFuzzySearch or useInfiniteScroll directly, add a comment; if not, make both local and update the barrel to NOT re-export (treat as internal). Principle: re-exports should be intentional, not accidental.

findings.title: Slides: til-briefing deck structure is well-organized; slides/ subdir is correct
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/slides/ (11x Slide*.vue), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/deck.ts (manifest, component imports, onMount hook), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/constellation.ts (canvas RAF loop), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/SlideFooter.vue (shared template), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/meta.ts (deck metadata)
findings.rootCause: The deck separates concerns correctly: (1) slides/ houses only .vue files with no cross-slide shared utilities, (2) deck.ts is the single manifest (order, dark mode flag, aria-labels, onMount effect), (3) constellation.ts is the shared effect (imported by deck.ts, not by slides), (4) SlideFooter is a sibling shared component, (5) meta.ts is deck metadata. Slides import only SlideFooter and useSlideContext (global). No cross-slide coupling.
findings.proposal: No changes. The til-briefing deck structure is idiomatic. Slides are stateless leaf components; orchestration and effects live in deck.ts. Scoped <style> blocks in each Slide are appropriate (per-slide visuals). CSS tokens live in /src/styles/deck.css (global). This is the correct flat structure for a deck-specific presentation.

findings.title: Slides: constellation.ts is well-colocated; no refactoring needed
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/constellation.ts (500+ lines, seeded PRNG for deterministic snapshots, Node/Constellation class, RAF loop, prefers-reduced-motion check), deck.ts imports and calls createConstellations(root) in onMount hook; no other slides import it
findings.rootCause: constellation.ts is a deck-level effect (not a shared composable, not a component). It is self-contained (no dependencies on other modules except for DOM/Canvas APIs) and is consumed only by deck.ts. Keeping it at the deck root alongside deck.ts and meta.ts is correct.
findings.proposal: No changes. This is well-organized. If the constellation effect becomes reusable across decks (e.g., feedback-coder also uses it), move it to /src/lib/constellation.ts. Until then, keep it deck-local.

risks: Consolidating lightweight components into /primitives/ may surprise users who expect Pulse.vue to live in Pulse/. Requires a clear migration guide or new API path (e.g., @mkbabb/glass-ui/components/primitives).
Moving Configurator.density.ts into composables/ is a renaming refactor; internal imports must be updated in Configurator.vue and ConfiguratorRow.vue.
Typewriter.utils consolidation requires deciding which utilities are public API; poorly chosen exports lock consumers into fragile dependencies.
The Search composables re-export decision is ambiguous; documenting it may expose a design inconsistency if the pattern was unintentional.

deferredItems.item: GU-003: Consolidate lightweight single-component directories into /primitives/
deferredItems.why: Low cohesion benefit for 2-file components; reduces directory clutter. However, team may prefer per-component directory mirroring for consistency. If adopted, requires registry + docs update. Defer until team consensus on the pattern.

deferredItems.item: GU-004: Typewriter index.ts barrel re-export of utils
deferredItems.why: Clarifies public API boundary. Low risk (internal refactor only). Depends on whether keyboard.ts, timing.ts, etc. are meant to be public. Requires typewriter README update.

deferredItems.item: GU-005: Configurator density.ts relocation to composables/
deferredItems.why: Clarifies context helper pattern but is purely cosmetic (renaming). Only pursue if team adopts a strict composables-only rule for provide/inject. Currently works fine at the root.

deferredItems.item: GU-006: Search vs. InfiniteScroll composables re-export consistency
deferredItems.why: Document the intent (are these public API or internal?). If internal, remove re-export and clarify in comments. If public, explain why only one is global. Low effort, high clarity.

findings.area: Vue 3.5 Pattern Adoption Audit (glass-ui + slides/til-briefing)
findings.summary: Audit of Vue 3.5 modernization patterns across glass-ui (539 files) and slides (58 files in til-briefing deck). Adoption is partially mature: defineModel is present but underutilized (3 instances vs. 8+ manual v-model emits); useTemplateRef is broadly adopted (15+ instances); defineSlots is completely absent; watchEffect is sparse (2 instances); defineExpose has moderate uptake (12 instances); toValue/MaybeRefOrGetter patterns are idiomatic in composables; watch() is the dominant choice over watchEffect for explicit dependencies. Conservative upgrade sites identified: 3 high-confidence defineModel candidates, 1 SearchBar ref-expose simplification, watch patterns within composables that could benefit from watchEffect in specific cases, and props destructuring that is safely reactive via computed/toValue.

findings.title: defineModel underadoption: 8+ manual v-model emit sites vs. 3 defineModel
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/multi-select/MultiSelect.vue:80,85 (emit('update:modelValue')); /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/tabs/BouncyTabs.vue:28-29; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/tabs/UnderlineTabs.vue:28-29; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/tabs/BouncyToggle.vue:57-59 vs. defineModel at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/confirm-dialog/ConfirmDialog.vue:64; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/expandable-container/ExpandableContainer.vue:91; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/DockLayerGroup.vue:38
findings.rootCause: defineModel (Vue 3.4+) consolidates props + emit patterns into single declaration; only 3 existing instances despite 8+ candidates showing manual emit('update:modelValue') or emit('update:open'). Inertia from pre-3.4 codebases.
findings.proposal: Convert MultiSelect, BouncyTabs, UnderlineTabs, BouncyToggle, SearchBar, ResponsiveTabs, and HoverPopover from manual defineProps + defineEmits to defineModel<T>(name, options). Each transforms (e.g., MultiSelect line 30-38 + 46 → const modelValue = defineModel<string[]>('modelValue'); const emit = defineEmits<{}>()). Isomorphic render — no behavior change.

findings.title: HoverPopover: manual sync watcher can fold into defineModel
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/hover-popover/HoverPopover.vue:156-166 (watch isOpen → emit update:open; watch props.open → sync isOpen)
findings.rootCause: Two-way binding via defineModel + internal watcher would collapse the dual-sync pattern into a single reactive source. Currently: props.open → watch → isOpen ref → watch → emit. defineModel collapses to: isOpen = defineModel<boolean>('open'); consumers read/write isOpen directly.
findings.proposal: Replace lines 40-54 (defineEmits) + 156-166 (dual watch) with `const isOpen = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })`. Removes 10 lines of watcher boilerplate while preserving exact same behavior for dock-keep-open (line 183) and native path (line 172) consumers. defineModel's two-way sync is automatic.

findings.title: SearchBar: ref expose can simplify to useTemplateRef
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/SearchBar.vue:41,43 (const inputRef = ref(...); defineExpose({ inputRef }))
findings.rootCause: SearchBar declares a template ref via manual ref(), then re-exports via defineExpose. useTemplateRef(name) replaces both patterns in a single declaration: const inputRef = useTemplateRef<HTMLInputElement>('inputRef'); the template binding + expose is implicit.
findings.proposal: Line 41: `const inputRef = useTemplateRef<HTMLInputElement>('inputRef')` replaces both line 41 (ref constructor) and line 43 (defineExpose). Import useTemplateRef from vue. Behavior identical; code is idiomatic 3.5.

findings.title: FuzzySearch: watch array of derived sources with watchEffect ergonomics
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/FuzzySearch.vue:47-63 (watch([...], () => { repaintHighlight(...) }, { flush: 'post' }))
findings.rootCause: watch([query, results, isExpanded, inlineOpen]) with a single side-effect callback (repaintHighlight). The array-of-sources pattern is necessary when tracking multiple independent reactives, but watchEffect could replace this for readability if the dependency graph is kept explicit via accessed values.
findings.proposal: This watch is idiomatic as-is (array of sources + explicit { flush: 'post' } for post-update timing). No change needed — the dependency array prevents over-triggering. If simplified to watchEffect, the automatic dependency tracking would require care to avoid accidental re-runs. KEEP as-is per KISS principle.

findings.title: ScrollingText: watchEffect used idomatically for auto-measure
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/scrolling-text/ScrollingText.vue:2,14,67 (import watchEffect; watchEffect(() => measure()))
findings.rootCause: ScrollingText.vue uses watchEffect to auto-run measure() whenever its dependencies change (containerRef, contentRef via template binding). This is the intended use case — 'effect' setup where side-effects are tied to reactive state implicitly. Pattern is modern + idiomatic.
findings.proposal: No change — ScrollingText already demonstrates Vue 3.5 watchEffect best practice. Cited as positive example of pattern adoption.

findings.title: toValue/MaybeRefOrGetter: mature adoption in composables
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/composables/sidebar/useSidebarState.ts:14,76,94,98,101-102 (import toValue; toValue(options.activeId)); /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/composables/sidebar/useScrollTracker.ts:9,62,77,167-168 (toValue(roots)); /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/infinite-scroll/composables/useInfiniteScroll.ts:1,17,57 (toValue(hasMore), toValue(isLoading))
findings.rootCause: Composables consistently accept MaybeRefOrGetter<T> and internally unwrap via toValue(). This decouples consumers from Ref constructor semantics — callers can pass raw values, getter functions, or Refs. Pattern is idiomatic + mature.
findings.proposal: No change — composable adoption is already modern. Documented as reference pattern for new composables.

findings.title: defineExpose discipline: 12 instances, all with static/computed payloads
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/carousel/Carousel.vue:14-22 (expose canScrollNext, canScrollPrev, carouselApi, ...); /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/goo-blob/GooBlob.vue:70; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/FuzzySearch.vue:66; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/GlassDock.vue:356
findings.rootCause: defineExpose is consistently used, but always exposes computed/method results — never raw mutable refs. This is the correct discipline (expose the contract, not internal state). No violations detected.
findings.proposal: No change — defineExpose usage is already mature and idiomatic. Continue enforcing pattern of exposing computed/methods, never raw refs.

findings.title: useTemplateRef: 15+ instances, broadly adopted
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/slider/Slider.vue:2,94; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/scrolling-text/ScrollingText.vue:14,44-45; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/goo-blob/GooBlob.vue:2,39-40; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dialog-native/GlassDialogNative.vue:2,46; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/GlassDock.vue:2,116-117; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/dock/DockLayerGroup.vue:2,42; /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/glass-carousel/GlassCarousel.vue:2,27,51
findings.rootCause: useTemplateRef was adopted early (Vue 3.5 feature stabilization). Pattern is widespread — no migration debt.
findings.proposal: No change — useTemplateRef adoption is already comprehensive. Continue as standard pattern for template ref binding.

findings.title: defineSlots: zero adoption, no candidates identified
findings.evidence: grep -r 'defineSlots' /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src returned no results
findings.rootCause: defineSlots (Vue 3.5, for TypeScript slot typing) has zero uptake. No components expose typed slots via defineSlots. This is not a code smell — most glass-ui components either accept unconstrained default slots or use implicit slot typing via JSDoc. TypeScript slot types are an advanced opt-in.
findings.proposal: No change — defineSlots is valuable only for components with complex, documented slot contracts (e.g., Table/Row with multi-slot choreography). glass-ui's slot patterns are simple enough that JSDoc comments (if any) suffice. Recommend defineSlots adoption only for new high-complexity components.

findings.title: ResponsiveTabs: manual emit can upgrade to defineModel
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/responsive-tabs/ResponsiveTabs.vue:82-84 (defineEmits<{ 'update:modelValue': [value: string] }>(); emit('update:modelValue', value))
findings.rootCause: Same pattern as MultiSelect / BouncyTabs. Manual emit('update:modelValue', value) at line 136 can fold into defineModel<string>('modelValue').
findings.proposal: Replace lines 77-84 (defineProps + defineEmits) with: const props = withDefaults(defineProps<ResponsiveTabsProps>(), {...}); const modelValue = defineModel<string>('modelValue'). Line 136 becomes: modelValue.value = value. Removes emit() call entirely.

findings.title: DataTable: manual sort/page emit can use defineModel
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/data-table/DataTable.vue:62-65 (defineEmits<{ 'update:page': [page: number]; 'update:sort': [sort: DataTableSort] }>); lines 150-162 (emit('update:sort', {...}))
findings.rootCause: DataTable emits two separate update events (sort + page) that are candidates for defineModel. Currently: `emit('update:sort', ...)` at line 153; `emit('update:page', ...)` at line 160. Could use defineModel<DataTableSort>('sort') + defineModel<number>('page').
findings.proposal: Add to DataTable's script: const sort = defineModel<DataTableSort | undefined>('sort'); const page = defineModel<number>('page'). Then replace emit('update:sort', ...) with sort.value = ...; emit('update:page', ...) with page.value = .... Consumers change from :sort @update:sort to v-model:sort; :page @update:page to v-model:page. Isomorphic.

findings.title: ConfiguratorLayer: manual open emit via defineModel
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/configurator/ConfiguratorLayer.vue (emit('update:open') pattern similar to HoverPopover/ConfirmDialog)
findings.rootCause: ConfiguratorLayer holds internalOpen ref + watches props.open (manual sync), similar to HoverPopover. Pattern is candidate for defineModel consolidation.
findings.proposal: Replace defineEmits + manual sync watcher with: const internalOpen = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: props.defaultOpen }). Simplifies dual-sync boilerplate.

findings.title: Slides (til-briefing): minimal Vue 3.5 pattern usage
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/SlideFooter.vue (simple composable usage, no v-model); /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/slides/Slide02.vue (template only, no setup script)
findings.rootCause: Slides deck is presentation-tier (minimal interactivity). SlideFooter uses useSlideContext() but no v-model, defineModel, or other stateful patterns. Components are template-heavy, logic-light.
findings.proposal: No action required — slides have no v-model patterns to migrate. If slides add complex interactive controls in future waves, apply glass-ui patterns as reference.

findings.title: Watch patterns: prefer explicit dependencies over watchEffect in state-sync
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/composables/sidebar/useScrollTracker.ts:175-182 (watch(() => toValue(roots), ...)); /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/hover-popover/HoverPopover.vue:158-162 (watch(() => props.open, ...)); /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/configurator/ConfiguratorLayer.vue (watch([isOpen, ...]))
findings.rootCause: Glass-ui consistently uses watch() with explicit dependency arrays or getter functions. watchEffect is reserved for side-effect-only patterns (e.g., ScrollingText measure). This discipline prevents over-triggering and makes dependencies visible.
findings.proposal: No change — current watch discipline is idiomatic. Continue preference for explicit dependencies. watchEffect is appropriate ONLY for 'fire whenever any tracked reactive value changes' semantics (e.g., effectful setup). Maintain distinction.

findings.title: InfiniteScroll: toRef computed pattern for MaybeRefOrGetter
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/infinite-scroll/InfiniteScroll.vue:28-29 (toRef(() => props.hasMore); toRef(() => props.isLoading))
findings.rootCause: InfiniteScroll uses toRef with getter function to adapt props to MaybeRefOrGetter shape. This is the correct pattern when a composable requires MaybeRefOrGetter but the consumer has props. Idiomatic + correct.
findings.proposal: No change — pattern is already modern. Cited as reference for similar scenarios (props → composable adapter).

risks: Upgrading manual v-model emits to defineModel requires coordinated change across template + script; validation must confirm bidirectional binding works in all test harnesses (test-utils auto-unwrap behavior).

Converting watch(() => props.open, ...) patterns to defineModel removes manual watcher; ensure defineModel's implicit two-way sync achieves identical timing (particularly for dock-keep-open behavior in HoverPopover).
defineModel + watch interplay: if a component uses defineModel and ALSO watches the model value for side-effects, the watcher must be on the model ref (not the old emit), or it will not fire.
SearchBar useTemplateRef migration: confirm that defineExpose({ inputRef }) behaves identically to explicit export when accessed via template ref or test harness.

DataTable dual-model upgrade (sort + page) is more complex due to optionality (sort can be undefined); ensure defineModel<DataTableSort | undefined> handles null/undefined correctly across v-model binding.

deferredItems.item: defineSlots adoption for complex slot-choreography components
deferredItems.why: defineSlots is a TypeScript-first feature for advanced slot typing. Glass-ui's current slot patterns (unconstrained default slots, simple pass-throughs) do not require defineSlots. Revisit only when designing components with 3+ interdependent named slots or complex render-function slot contracts.

deferredItems.item: watchEffect adoption for imperative side-effects
deferredItems.why: watchEffect is correctly used in ScrollingText (measure callback). No broad adoption needed — watch() with explicit dependencies is the preferred discipline for state management. watchEffect adoption should be case-by-case, not systematic.

deferredItems.item: ConfiguratorLayer defineModel upgrade
deferredItems.why: Upgrade is idiomatic but depends on landing of HoverPopover + ConfirmDialog defineModel changes first (establishes pattern precedent). Schedule for wave after initial defineModel rollout (GU.W9 → GU.W10).

findings.area: glass-ui: Non-idiomatic Tailwind CSS v4 patterns audit
findings.summary: Audit of glass-ui Vue SFCs identified 12 primary non-idiomatic Tailwind patterns: excessive arbitrary values wrapping CSS variables, repeated magic numbers in fixed pixel widths/heights that should be tokens, complex compound selectors that should be @utility recipes, transition-property enums embedded in arbitrary values, and color values accessed via CSS vars in brackets instead of theme tokens. The codebase already has a solid theme infrastructure (tokens.css → theme.css @theme block) but 78+ component files leak implementation details into class strings. Most patterns can be resolved via new @theme entries, @utility recipes, or lift-and-repeat token references.

findings.title: CSS variable values in arbitrary brackets instead of @theme tokens
findings.evidence:
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/card/CardDescription.vue:11 — text-[var(--muted-foreground-strong)]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/drawer/DrawerOverlay.vue:17 — [backdrop-filter:var(--glass-blur-wash)]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/tabs/TabsTrigger.vue:22 — data-[state=active]:text-[var(--active-tab-color,var(--foreground))]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/carousel/CarouselDots.vue:71 — bg-[var(--muted-medium)]
findings.rootCause: CSS custom property literals are wrapped in Tailwind arbitrary-value brackets instead of being declared as @theme entries in theme.css. This prevents Tailwind from optimizing the output and requires runtime CSS var resolution.
findings.proposal: For each CSS var used in arbitrary brackets, add a @theme entry to src/styles/theme.css. Example: `--color-muted-foreground-strong: var(--muted-foreground-strong);` already exists in the @theme block (line 100+). Components should use `text-muted-foreground-strong` instead of `text-[var(--muted-foreground-strong)]`. For backdrop-filter, add `--backdrop-glass-blur-wash: var(--glass-blur-wash);` and use `backdrop-[blur-wash]` or create a dedicated @utility.

findings.title: Fixed pixel widths/heights (200px, 300px, 60vh, 70vh) should be tokens
findings.evidence:
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/combobox/ComboboxList.vue:24 — w-[200px]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/combobox/ComboboxAnchor.vue:19 — w-[200px]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/combobox/ComboboxViewport.vue:19 — max-h-[300px]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/command/CommandList.vue:22 — max-h-[300px]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/dropdown-menu/DropdownMenuContent.vue:37 — max-h-[60vh]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/FuzzySearch.vue:132 — max-h-[50vh]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/FuzzySearch.vue:148 — max-h-[70vh] !max-w-[36rem] !top-[12vh]
findings.rootCause: Magic numbers appear repeatedly across components. 200px for combobox width is reused at least 2 places; 300px for viewport height appears 2+ times; vh units (50vh, 60vh, 70vh, 12vh) are ad-hoc. These should be centralized tokens to enable consistent responsive scaling across the design system.
findings.proposal:
Add sizing tokens to tokens.css and @theme block:
- `--size-combobox-width: 200px;` → `w-combobox` utility
- `--size-popover-max-height: 300px;` → `max-h-popover` utility
- `--size-search-expanded-height: 70vh;` → `h-search-modal` utility
- `--size-search-compact-height: 50vh;` → `h-search-compact` utility
Then refactor components to use named utilities instead of arbitrary values. These are design decisions, not layout accidents.

findings.title: Compound arbitrary transition properties should be @utility recipes
findings.evidence:
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/carousel/CarouselDots.vue:62 — transition-[background-color,transform,width,height,box-shadow] duration-[var(--duration-fast)]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/accordion/AccordionContent.vue:18 — transition-[height,opacity] data-[state=closed]:animate-accordion-up
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/collapsible/CollapsibleContent.vue:8 — transition-[height,opacity] data-[state=closed]:animate-collapsible-up
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/tabs/TabsIndicator.vue:18 — transition-[width,transform]
findings.rootCause: Repeated multi-property transition enums are embedded as arbitrary values. These represent idiomatic animation recipes (e.g., 'height+opacity on collapse'), not one-offs. They should be extracted to @utility declarations for reuse and semantic clarity.

findings.title: Repeated data-slot selector chains should use @layer components recipe
findings.evidence:
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/command/CommandDialog.vue:16 — long chain of `[&_[cmdk-group-heading]]:px-2 [&_[cmdk-group-heading]]:font-medium [&_[cmdk-group-heading]]:text-muted-foreground ...` (8 selectors deep)
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/command/CommandGroup.vue:22 — similar pattern with `[&_[cmdk-group-heading]]:` repeated 4x
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/table/TableHeader.vue:11 — [&_tr]:border-b (repeated across table files)
findings.rootCause: Complex child-selector combinator chains are written as multiple arbitrary-value utilities instead of composed into named @layer components rules. This inflates the class string and obscures the semantic structure (e.g., 'Command dialog's child cmdk-group-heading styles').

findings.title: Bare CSS variable references should use data-attribute overrides or theme tokens
findings.evidence:
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/carousel/CarouselNext.vue:25, 27-28 — h-[var(--carousel-nav-size)] w-[var(--carousel-nav-size)] right-[calc(-1*var(--carousel-nav-offset))]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/select/SelectContent.vue:55 — h-[--reka-select-trigger-height] w-full min-w-[--reka-select-trigger-width]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/FuzzySearch.vue:132 — w-[var(--reka-popover-trigger-width)]
findings.rootCause: CSS custom properties (some reka-ui-injected, some locally defined) are referenced via arbitrary-value brackets. This works at runtime but doesn't benefit from Tailwind's static analysis or zero-cost abstractions. Reka-ui injected properties (--reka-*) cannot be pre-declared in @theme but should be documented and wrapped in @layer utilities.

findings.title: Icon size literals (0.6rem, 0.65rem) should be a sizing scale token
findings.evidence:
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/FuzzySearch.vue:139 — text-[0.6rem]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/FuzzySearch.vue:165 — text-[0.65rem]
findings.rootCause: Two near-identical font sizes (0.6rem vs 0.65rem) are hardcoded in Badge components within FuzzySearch. These appear to be intentional micro-scale variants (compact vs expanded search UI) but are expressed as arbitrary values instead of a named token pair.
findings.proposal:
Add to tokens.css:
```css
--type-badge-compact: 0.6rem;  /* 9.6px, FuzzySearch inline badge */
--type-badge-modal: 0.65rem;   /* 10.4px, FuzzySearch modal badge */
```
Add to @theme: `--text-badge-compact` and `--text-badge-modal`, exposing `text-badge-compact` / `text-badge-modal` utilities. Refactor FuzzySearch to bind these based on `isExpanded.value` context.

findings.title: Calc expressions (100%-2rem, -1*var) should be token-backed or @utility recipes
findings.evidence:
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/confirm-dialog/ConfirmDialog.vue:12 — w-[calc(100%-2rem)]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/carousel/CarouselNext.vue:27 — right-[calc(-1*var(--carousel-nav-offset))]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/carousel/CarouselPrevious.vue:27 — left-[calc(-1*var(--carousel-nav-offset))]
findings.rootCause: Calc expressions embed layout logic in class strings. The 100%-2rem pattern (modal dialog width with gutters) and -1*var patterns (carousel nav positioning) are layout decisions, not arbitrary one-offs.

findings.title: Shadow utility wrapping CSS variable should be @theme token
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/card/Card.vue:73 — shadow-[var(--shadow-card)]
findings.rootCause: The shadow value is stored in a CSS variable (--shadow-card) but accessed via an arbitrary-value utility instead of a Tailwind @theme shadow token. This prevents Tailwind from recognizing it as a shadow utility for static analysis.
findings.proposal:
Add to @theme block in theme.css:
```css
--shadow-card: var(--shadow-card);  /* or map directly to the resolved value */
```
Then use `shadow-card` (a named Tailwind shadow) instead of `shadow-[var(--shadow-card)]`. This is already partially done in theme.css line 90 (`--color-shadow: var(--shadow);`), but card-specific shadow needs exposure.

findings.title: Modal positioning magic numbers should be token-based
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/search/FuzzySearch.vue:148 — !top-[12vh] !translate-y-0
findings.rootCause: The search modal dialog's vertical anchor (12vh from top) is a magic number hardcoded in the class string. This layout decision should be parameterized so it can be adjusted globally or per breakpoint.
findings.proposal:
Add a token for modal top position:
```css
--position-modal-top: 12vh;
```
Expose via @theme and use `top-modal` utility. If response across viewport heights is needed, consider a CSS custom property bound to a viewport query or @container rule.

findings.title: Separator thickness (1px) and label dimensions should be tokens
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/separator/Separator.vue:31 — w-[1px] py-1 px-2 (for label area) and h-[1px] (for line)
findings.rootCause: Separator uses bare 1px for thickness and hardcoded padding (py-1 px-2) for the label container. While 1px is standard, the label container dimensions are orthogonal design decisions that should be centralized.
findings.proposal:
Add to tokens.css:
```css
--size-separator-thickness: 1px;
--size-separator-label-py: 0.5rem;  /* py-2 = 0.5rem * 2 */
--size-separator-label-px: 0.5rem;  /* px-2 = 0.5rem * 2 */
```
But honestly, for such tiny values, the current approach is acceptable. This is P3 — lower priority than structural refactors.

findings.title: Negative margin/translate using CSS variables should use @utility pattern
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/custom/stacked-icons/StackedIconGroup.vue:87-95 — `-mt-[var(--stack-overlap-sm)] -mt-[var(--stack-overlap-md)] -mt-[var(--stack-overlap-lg)]` and parallel `-ml-[var(...)]`
findings.rootCause: Margin negation patterns are repeated for 3 size tiers (sm/md/lg) × 2 directions (vertical/horizontal). This is a CVA variant set that should be extracted to @utility or a component class.

findings.title: Transition duration/ease arbitrary values should reference existing tokens consistently
findings.evidence:
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/tabs/TabsTrigger.vue:22 — duration-[var(--duration-fast)] ease-[var(--ease-standard)]
/Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src/components/ui/tabs/TabsIndicator.vue:18 — duration-[var(--duration-normal)] ease-[var(--spring-snappy)]

findings.rootCause: Transition durations and easings are always accessed via CSS variables in arbitrary brackets instead of Tailwind @theme durations and animations. This is inconsistent with the library's theme infrastructure and prevents Tailwind from optimizing duration/easing across the build.

risks: Refactoring arbitrary values to @theme tokens requires updates to the theme.css @theme block; any typo or missing token will break the build. Recommend testing theme block syntax with `tailwindcss --build` before deploying.

Moving complex selectors from arbitrary values to @layer components rules may interact unpredictably with component-scoped styles in Vue if CSS specificity is not carefully managed. Test collision-free composition with existing consumer styles.

Some reka-ui-injected CSS variables (--reka-*) are runtime-injected and cannot be pre-declared in @theme; accepting the arbitrary-value pattern for these is correct but requires explicit documentation in comments to prevent future audits from re-flagging.

Magic number refactor (200px, 300px, 60vh) may affect component intrinsic sizing in edge cases if these dimensions were previously hard-coded by design. Recommend spot-checking responsive layouts after token lift.

The magic number for modal top position (12vh) may need adjustment for accessibility (e.g., focus visible buttons at the modal bottom should not be cut off). Consider adding a CSS variable with a @supports fallback.

@utility recipes created for transition properties must be carefully named to avoid collision with Tailwind's built-in utilities (e.g., `collapse-animate` vs. Tailwind's `animate-` naming convention). Recommend prefixing custom animation utilities with a scope (e.g., `.gl-collapse-animate`).

deferredItems.item: GU-13: Vendor-specific backdrop-filter arbitrary value pattern
deferredItems.why: Backdrop-filter is a CSS standard property but Tailwind's @theme does not natively expose a `backdrop-filter` utility family. This arbitrary value is acceptable but should be wrapped in a @layer component or @utility to document why it's raw CSS. Consider: does glass-ui have a dedicated backdrop-blur-wash utility already? If not, add one to utilities.css with a comment explaining the vendor prefix handling.

deferredItems.item: GU-14: Toast/notification position hardcoding (bottom-4 right-4, etc.)
deferredItems.source:
