This is idiomatic Tailwind usage; the VIEWPORT_ANCHOR record is a data structure, not a class string smell. Position utilities (bottom-4, right-4) are appropriate here. No refactor needed unless users request custom anchor points, at which point the component can expose a `position` prop (which Toaster already does at line 22).

deferredItems.why: These are idiomatic Tailwind opacity utilities and correctly use the native scale. No arbitrary values here. Dialog close button (opacity-70 → opacity-100 on hover) and select checkmarks (opacity-0 → opacity-100 for visibility toggle) are UI patterns that benefit from explicit opacity values. No refactor needed.

findings.area: Tailwind / Deck Utility Idiom Audit
findings.summary: Audit of til-briefing SFCs revealed 8 categories of non-idiomatic styling: (1) arbitrary color-mix tints scattered across 5+ slides that should be a unified deck palette (e.g., --cream-tint-{6,7,8,9,10,12}, --red-glow-{4,12,22,30,45}); (2) inline text-shadow and box-shadow expressions with specific red color-mix blurs that duplicate—should be --shadow-red-glow-{sm,md,lg}; (3) SVG element classes (.ic, .cg, .stroke, .faint, .halo, .outlier) redefined per-slide instead of unified deck utilities; (4) three inline style= attributes (Slide01, Slide07×2, Slide09) that bypass scoped CSS; (5) hard-coded #000 in mask-image gradients across 5 slides (Slides 01, 04, 05, 07, 10) that should use a token; (6) bespoke cartoon offset shadows with color-mix blending not yet parameterized; (7) filter drop-shadow glows without a utility abstraction; (8) SVG class duplication (.ic/.ic-fill/.cg/.cg-fill/.stroke/.faint) across Slides 03, 06, 08, 09. All patterns are isomorphic rewrites—no functional change, purely idiom/token lifting.

findings.title: Arbitrary color-mix() tints scattered across slides—should be unified deck utility palette
findings.evidence: Slide04:148–150 (.bar-track/.bar-contract/.bar-billed fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cream-on-ink) {8,42}%, transparent)); Slide07:170–171 (background gradient with --cream-on-ink {9,22}%); Slide11:155,172–173,176,187 (border/background with --cream-on-ink {6,7,10,14,22}%). Similar pattern for red: Slide07:151 (text-shadow, --ncsu-red 45%), Slide07:191 (box-shadow, --ncsu-red 60%), Slide04:173 (radial-gradient, --ncsu-red 30%), etc.
findings.rootCause: No centralized tint register in deck.css for opacity-reduced variants of key tokens (cream-on-ink, ncsu-red). Each slide authors its own color-mix() at point of use, creating fragmentation.
findings.proposal: Lift tint palette to deck.css as --cream-tint-{6,7,8,9,10,12,14,16,22} and --red-tint-{4,12,22,30,45,50,55,58,60,72} utility variables. Rewrite all inline color-mix() to reference tokens. Isomorphic: no visual change, purely token abstraction.

findings.title: Inline text-shadow and box-shadow with red color-mix glows should be deck @utilities
findings.evidence: Slide07:151 (.fig__n text-shadow: 0 0 26px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 45%, transparent)); Slide07:214 (.ratio__x text-shadow: 0 0 22px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 50%, transparent)); Slide07:191 (box-shadow: 0 0 30px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 60%, transparent)); Slide07:243 (.gauge__big text-shadow: 0 0 42px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 58%, transparent)); Slide11:166 (a.window:hover box-shadow includes color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 55%, transparent)).
findings.rootCause: Glow effects (red-tinted blur shadows) are hand-authored inline per-use, creating repetition and inconsistent blur/opacity pairs. No abstract shadow glows register in deck.css.
findings.proposal: Add deck-level shadow utility tokens: --shadow-red-glow-sm: 0 0 22px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 45%, transparent); --shadow-red-glow-md: 0 0 26px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 50%, transparent); --shadow-red-glow-lg: 0 0 42px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 58%, transparent). Replace all inline instances with var(--shadow-red-glow-*). Isomorphic: purely token ref substitution.

findings.title: SVG element classes (.ic, .cg, .stroke, .faint, .halo, .outlier) redefined per-slide instead of unified deck utilities
findings.evidence: Slide03:212–216 (.glyph .stroke { stroke: var(--ncsu-red); stroke-width: 1.6; ... }, .glyph .faint, .glyph .halo, .glyph .outlier); Slide06:311–312 (.ic { fill: none; stroke: currentColor; ... }, .ic-fill { fill: currentColor; }); Slide08:311–312 (identical .ic/.ic-fill rules); Slide09:269–270 (.cg { fill: none; stroke: var(--ncsu-red); ... }, .cg-fill { fill: var(--ncsu-red); }). Each slide re-declares the same SVG styling idioms.
findings.rootCause: No deck-level SVG utility class layer; each slide scopes its own icon styling rules, leading to duplication across Slides 03, 06, 08, 09.
findings.proposal: Lift all SVG element classes to deck.css: .ic (no-fill stroke), .ic-fill (solid fill), .svg-stroke-red (stroke: var(--ncsu-red)), .svg-faint (opacity: 0.32), .svg-halo (opacity: 0.18), etc. Update all scoped rules to remove duplicates and reference deck utilities. Isomorphic: consolidation only, no visual change.

findings.title: Hard-coded #000 in mask-image gradients should use a token
findings.evidence: Slide01:69,198 (mask-image: linear-gradient(..., #000 0%, #000 46%, ...)); Slide04:102 (linear-gradient(105deg, transparent 38%, #000 78%, ...)); Slide05:119 (linear-gradient(200deg, #000 8%, ...)); Slide07:132 (linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 0%, #000 40%, ...)); Slide10:96 (linear-gradient(255deg, #000 0%, #000 40%, ...)).
findings.rootCause: Mask gradients use bare color #000 for opaque regions instead of a semantic token that could adapt to dark mode or be centrally adjusted.
findings.proposal: Define --mask-opaque: #000 in deck.css and replace all bare #000 in mask-image with var(--mask-opaque). Isomorphic: purely token substitution, no visual difference.

findings.title: Inline style= attributes bypass scoped CSS and should use classes
findings.evidence: Slide01:18 (style="--crest-size: clamp(...)") — CSS custom prop assignment (acceptable but better as scoped class); Slide07:31 (style="margin:0") — hard-coded margin override; Slide09:61 (style="overflow:visible") — SVG-only, but inline.
findings.rootCause: Inline styles for one-off property overrides instead of using scoped class definitions or utility tokens.
findings.proposal: Move Slide07:31 margin:0 to .display-clean { margin: 0; } class (already present in template but using inline instead). Slide09:61 overflow:visible can remain inline (SVG context) or move to .wave--overflow-visible class. Slide01:18 crest-size is a dynamic CSS custom prop—acceptable inline but could scope to .til-crest { --crest-size: clamp(...); }. Isomorphic: class relocation only.

findings.title: Cartoon offset shadows with color-mix blending not yet parameterized
findings.evidence: Slide05:257 (box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 0 ...) and Slide08:304 (box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 0 color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 22%, transparent)) use bespoke cartoon shadow with red tint. deck.css already has --shadow-cartoon-red (line 117) but these are local variants mixing color-mix opacity.
findings.rootCause: Cartoon shadow variants with specific opacity (22%) are authored inline per-slide instead of as parameterized utilities.
findings.proposal: Define --shadow-cartoon-red-dark: 4px 4px 0 0 color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 22%, transparent) in deck.css and reference via var(). Or create utility class .shadow-cartoon-red-dark { box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-red-dark); }. Isomorphic: token lifting.

findings.title: Filter drop-shadow glows (arc glow) lack a reusable utility abstraction
findings.evidence: Slide07:230 (.arc-fill { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 18px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 72%, transparent)); }) — a bespoke filter expression for the progress arc glow.
findings.rootCause: No filter utility register in deck.css for drop-shadow glows; authored inline per-slide.
findings.proposal: Add deck utility --filter-red-glow: drop-shadow(0 0 18px color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 72%, transparent)) and replace inline filter with filter: var(--filter-red-glow). Isomorphic: token substitution.

findings.title: SVG class namespace collision and duplication (.ic, .cg, .stroke, .faint) across multiple slides
findings.evidence: Slide03 defines .glyph .stroke, .glyph .faint, .glyph .halo, .glyph .outlier (lines 212–216). Slide06 defines .ic, .ic-fill (lines 311–312). Slide08 redefines .ic, .ic-fill identically (lines 311–312). Slide09 defines .cg, .cg-fill (lines 269–270). All slides reuse these class names without cross-slide coordination.
findings.rootCause: Scoped CSS per-slide allows name reuse but creates cognitive load and maintenance risk if rules ever diverge. No single source of truth for SVG styling idioms.
findings.proposal: Consolidate all SVG utility classes (.ic, .ic-fill, .svg-stroke-red, .svg-faint, .svg-halo, .svg-outlier) into deck.css and import/apply throughout. Update all slide scoped styles to remove duplicates. Isomorphic: consolidation, no visual change.

risks: Risk of introducing visual regressions if token values are miscalibrated (e.g., blur radius or opacity in drop-shadow). Mitigation: pixel-perfect comparison in a test export before commit.

Risk of breaking glass-ui inheritance if deck.css tokens override upstream in conflicting ways. Mitigation: verify all new tokens use light-dark() parity with deck's existing style (e.g., --shadow-red-glow should have dark-mode variant).
Risk of SVG class lift affecting performance if deck.css grows significantly. Mitigation: SVG utility classes are ~5KB of additional CSS; acceptable within deck scale.

findings.area: Monolithic stylesheet audit: SL/src/styles/deck.css (F.W7 target) and GU/src/styles file organization
findings.summary: SL/src/styles/deck.css (902 lines) is correctly organized as a monolithic design-system spine with legitimate global scope: §1 tokens (custom properties for the deck's identity), §3 typography (the φ golden-ratio ladder), §6 chrome (slide header/footer/dock positioning), §8 dock/progress (the floating control bar), and entrance choreography. Slide-specific layout/composition rules correctly live in per-slide <style scoped> blocks. The deck's architecture is already optimal. GU/src/styles demonstrates a healthy component-layered pattern: glass.css (5-tier surface ladder, 360 lines), dock.css (1200 lines of component rules within @layer components), and animations.css (375 lines of shared @keyframes) are correctly global. However, dock.css should split its 800+ lines of density tokens and layout variants into a separate file to improve maintainability (the base glass-dock surface belongs with glass.css; density presets and controls belong in dock-controls.css). The animations.css file is pure @keyframes (legitimately global) with no component specifics leaking.

findings.title: GU/src/styles/glass.css is correctly global: 5-tier surface ladder + accessibility gates
findings.evidence: glass.css:1-97 (.glass-{wash,quiet,resting,floating,overlay} tier series + .glass-card/.glass-btn + grain + blend-mode toggle); 295-323 (@media prefers-reduced-transparency/contrast); 355-360 (@supports fallback). Zero component-specifics; pure design-system tokens materialized as Tailwind @layer components.
findings.rootCause: N/A—this is correct architecture.
findings.proposal: Keep as-is. This is the canonical glass surface abstraction—no redesign needed.

findings.title: GU/src/styles/dock.css violates KISS: 1200 lines of mixed concerns (surface + 800 lines of density/control variants)
findings.evidence: dock.css:8-179 (legitimate: .glass-dock base surface + density states [compact/comfortable/spacious/audacious]); 180-1200 (controls: .dock-icon-button, .dock-tab-button, .dock-select-trigger, .dock-dropdown-trigger + .dark-mode-toggle-button + @media density carves). Density tokens at :91-163 and controls at :730-1103 are load-bearing but orthogonal concerns.
findings.rootCause: All dock-family selectors bundled into a monolith to keep the cascade order deterministic (tokens → surface → controls). The file compresses four distinct subsystems: (1) .glass-dock base + @layer, (2) .dock-density-* preset rules, (3) .dock-icon/tab/select/dropdown-button family, (4) .dark-mode-toggle. Splitting without care breaks the token-reading order.
findings.proposal: SPLIT into THREE files (no output-size penalty; gzip already deduplicates): (a) dock.css (current :8-179, :1135-1159) = .glass-dock surface + base layout + density presets—the shell. (b) dock-controls.css = .dock-icon-button / .dock-tab-button / .dock-select-trigger / .dock-dropdown-trigger + .dark-mode-toggle (current :730-1103)—the control family. (c) KEEP animations.css unlayered but wrap dock-specific @media blocks (density carves at :154-163) into dock.css (they are surface-only, not control-specific). Import order: tokens → glass → dock → dock-controls → animations. The control file reads all tokens + .glass-dock class names (no circular dep). This lifts each concern to read-at-a-glance size and unblocks async work.

findings.title: GU/src/styles/animations.css is correctly global: 23 @keyframes with shared motion vocabulary, zero component leakage
findings.evidence: animations.css:1-376. All @keyframes are named primitives (floating-panel-in, collapsible-open, fade-in, shake, sparkle-sweep, etc.), consumed by component <style scoped> blocks (not declared there). The [data-scrim-animation] cascade rule (:290-298) is a PORTALED-ELEMENT exception—the reka-ui DialogPortal teleports the overlay outside the component subtree, so a consumer's scoped style never reaches it; the rule must be global. Reduced-motion gating is declared at both the @keyframes AND the consumer site (defensive).
findings.rootCause: N/A—this is correct architecture.
findings.proposal: Keep as-is. This is the canonical shared-animation library. The [data-scrim-animation] rule is a justified exception to the component-scoped discipline. Document the rationale in a header comment (already present at :260-288, good).

findings.title: SL/src/styles/deck.css is correctly monolithic: five LEGITIMATE global concerns (tokens + type + chrome + dock/progress + choreography)
findings.evidence: deck.css §1 (lines 20-136): root CSS custom properties — :root { --ncsu-red, --ai-blue-*, --portal-*, --card, --radius-*, --glass-highlight, --font-*, --type-*, --lead-*, --track-*, --shadow-*, --ease-*, --spring-* }. All deck-wide tokens, zero component specifics. §3 (lines 336-397): .text-{display-2,title,heading,prose,body,small,caption}, .mono, .eyebrow, .section-label, typography utilities. §6 (lines 492-523): .slide__header, .slide__footer, .slide__num, .til-mark, .til-crest — slide chrome. §8 (lines 560-814): .deck-dock-wrap, .deck-dock, .deck-pager, .deck-progress, .deck-settings, .deck-edge, .deck-gate — the floating dock + progress bar + access gate (teleported globals). §7 (lines 525-554): @keyframes {rise, fade, wipe-x, grow-y} + [data-reveal] entrance choreography.
findings.rootCause: N/A—this is correct architecture.
findings.proposal: Keep as-is. The deck.css monolith is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the slide-system identity. Moving tokens/type/chrome piecemeal to per-slide scopes would fragment the cascade and force every slide to re-import shared declarations. The design-spine MUST be global; slide-specific layout lives in per-slide <style scoped> (Slide06.vue:120-200, Slide08.vue, Slide11.vue:120+)—correctly colocated. The print/export/dark-mode sections (§9, §10) are legitimately global (they gate the entire deck, not per-component). No redesign needed.

findings.title: SL/src/styles/deck.css §6 chrome selectors are slide-layout-adjacent, not truly component-scoped—correct placement
findings.evidence: deck.css:492-523 (.slide__header, .slide__footer, .slide__num, .til-mark, .til-crest). These are consumed by every slide and SlideFooter.vue (a reusable component). The deck owns the rhythm (header margin 1.5rem, footer margin-top auto, footer font). Per-slide customization (e.g., Slide06's padding override at Slide06.vue:126) is scoped.
findings.rootCause: These are layout-transport rules: every slide carries them, but no slide redefines them—they inherit deck defaults. A shared component (SlideFooter.vue) consumes .til-mark and .til-crest, so they cannot be per-slide.
findings.proposal: Rename .slide__header → .slide-header and .slide__footer → .slide-footer (idiomatic BEM parallel to .slide-dock, .slide-progress) for clarity that they are layout fixtures, not private component slots. No functional change; the rules stay global. This lifts the semantics: __header reads as 'header slot'; -header reads as 'the header bar construct'—the latter is more durable. Pair the rename with a comment: '/* Global slide chrome — every .slide inherits these. Per-slide customization lives in <style scoped>. */'.

findings.title: SL/src/styles/deck.css §7 entrance choreography (@keyframes rise/fade/wipe-x + [data-reveal]) is correctly global: every slide consumes this
findings.evidence: deck.css:525-554 (@keyframes rise/fade/wipe-x/grow-y + [data-reveal] animation bindings + reduced-motion gate). Every slide uses v-reveal and v-reveal:fade directives; the stagger formula (calc(var(--d, 0) * 0.09s + 0.12s)) is deck-canonical.
findings.rootCause: N/A—this is correct.
findings.proposal: Keep as-is. This is the entrance orchestration for the reveal system; it must be global so every slide's [data-reveal] elements resolve to the same keyframe canon.

findings.title: SL/src/styles/deck.css §8 dock/progress/gate rules are correctly global: teleported components + viewport-pinned chrome
findings.evidence: deck.css:560-814 (.deck-dock-wrap, .deck-dock, .deck-pager, .deck-progress, .deck-settings, .deck-edge, .deck-gate). The .deck-dock-wrap pins the GlassDock at fixed/bottom (line 573); .deck-pager and .deck-progress are slide-decoupled. .deck-settings and .deck-gate are teleported (reka-ui Portal), so scoped styles cannot reach them (line 737 comment: 'GLOBAL: the Dialog content is teleported out of the component subtree'). The edge-zone arrows (.deck-edge) are top:0/bottom:0 fixed elements, deck-state-aware (line 786).
findings.rootCause: Teleported elements and viewport-pinned chrome CANNOT be component-scoped. A scoped <style> only reaches its own component's subtree; the portal empties it before style resolution. A reka-ui Dialog's content is portaled to a separate tree root, so .deck-gate rules MUST live globally.
findings.proposal: Keep as-is. These rules cannot be moved without breaking the teleportation. The comment at line 737 is accurate. Consider a header comment on the entire §8 block: '/* Deck viewport chrome — dock, progress, and portaled gates. Teleported elements (DeckSettings, DeckGate) sit outside component subtrees, so these rules must be global. Per-slide customization hooks via CSS custom properties (e.g., --deck-dock-clearance, --deck-pager-fit). */'

risks: Splitting dock.css (GU-2) requires careful @import order discipline: glass.css must load before dock-controls.css so .glass-dock base rules are available. Verify in glass-ui/src/styles/index.css that the cascade order is documented and immutable.

The [data-scrim-animation] rule in animations.css (SL-3, GU-3) depends on a producer writing --scrim-animation to the inline style. If a consumer mistakenly tries a scoped <style> rule instead of the global fallback, the rule won't fire. Document the pattern in ModalOverlay's JSDoc.

Renaming .slide__header → .slide-header (SL-2) is a VISUAL change only if BEM strict; verify that no external consumers (PPTX export, print CSS, automation) depend on the double-underscore selector. Git grep for __header in slides/ and dist/.

deferredItems.item: Profile @layer cascade order in glass-ui consumers to detect specificity inversions
deferredItems.why: The split is safe because dock-controls.css selectors (.dock-icon-button, etc.) have LOWER specificity than .glass-dock + [data-density] cascades, so load order never produces a conflict. But a profile run during F.W8 would validate the assumption and catch any future inversions early. Use CSS Specificity Tree (csstat) in CI.

deferredItems.item: Audit all per-slide <style scoped> blocks for @import or @keyframes leakage
deferredItems.why: Scoped CSS does not reach @keyframes declared inside it (they are hoisted), but the audit ensures no slide accidentally re-declares entrance choreography. A grep for '@keyframes' in slides/*.vue would be a quick smoke test; none should exist (entrance is deck-global per design).

findings.area: CSS modernization and deprecated pattern cleanup
findings.summary: Audit of both repos identified 9 deprecated CSS patterns requiring modernization: unnecessary vendor prefixes for widely-supported features, legacy color function mixins, double-wrapped color channels, and viewport-based media queries that should be container queries. Glass-ui's hsl(var(--background) / α) pattern in animations.css is correct per CLAUDE.md's channel-form rule but misleading in comments. Slides deck uses landscape-era webkit prefixes for scrollbars and printing. No float layouts or old flexbox syntax found; modern color-mix and light-dark() are already in use.

findings.title: Unnecessary -webkit-backdrop-filter fallback for widely-supported CSS
findings.evidence: glass-ui/src/styles/glass.css:326; glass-ui/src/composables/glass/useGlassRenderer.ts:lines with -webkit-backdrop-filter
findings.rootCause: backdrop-filter has been stable Baseline CSS since 2023; the @supports guard gates logic correctly but the -webkit- prefix is no longer needed in shipping browsers
findings.proposal: Remove -webkit-backdrop-filter property and the @supports fallback entirely. Keep @supports only for non-backdrop-filter browsers that need a solid-color fallback surface.

findings.title: Legacy -webkit-scrollbar pseudo-elements used outside proper @supports guard
findings.evidence: glass-ui/src/styles/utilities.css:111-137; dock.css scrollbar selectors; tokens.css comment §2a (lines mentioning scrollbar)
findings.rootCause: scrollbar-color + scrollbar-width are Baseline CSS (Chromium 121+); the webkit fallback is correctly @supports-gated for older browsers but utilities.css:111 has an ungated .scrollbar-hidden::-webkit-scrollbar rule
findings.proposal: Move .scrollbar-hidden::-webkit-scrollbar into the same @supports not (scrollbar-color) guard as the .scrollbar-thin rules. Modern engines use scrollbar-width/color only.

findings.title: Raw rgb(255 255 255) light-mode highlights instead of color-mix via token
findings.evidence: glass-ui/src/styles/instrument-rail.css:lines ~40-45; instrument-chassis.css bezel-line rules; tokens.css §7 shadow-cartoon-color definitions
findings.rootCause: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.10) hardcoded for white overlays instead of composing via a custom property so consumers cannot override the accent color for light highlights
findings.proposal: Extract into tokens.css as --highlight-overlay: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.10) and --highlight-overlay-subtle: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.06), then reference via var() in component CSS. Follows the --shadow-cartoon-color pattern already in place.

findings.title: -webkit-mask-image paired with modern mask-image (correct but verbose)
findings.evidence: glass-ui/src/styles/utilities.css:scroll-fade-mask, scroll-fade-top, scroll-fade-bottom, scroll-fade-y classes (4 rules, each with dual mask-image + -webkit-mask-image)
findings.rootCause: mask-image is Baseline CSS; -webkit- fallback is unnecessary for modern browsers. Prefixes are correct for older Safari but duplicate the definition 4 times.
findings.proposal: Keep the modern mask-image rule; remove all -webkit-mask-image lines. Safari 15+ ships unprefixed; pre-15 users receive no fade effect (graceful degradation). If pre-15 Safari support is binding, gate the webkit rules under @supports not (mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, transparent, black)).

findings.title: -webkit-background-clip: text for gradient-text utility (required for compatibility)
findings.evidence: glass-ui/src/styles/utilities.css:rainbow-text rule, background-clip + -webkit-background-clip pairing
findings.rootCause: background-clip: text is standard CSS but requires -webkit- fallback in Firefox and older Chromium. This is one of the rare cases where the prefix is still needed.
findings.proposal: Keep both. This is a load-bearing prefix; no change warranted. Document as an exception in CLAUDE.md if needed.

findings.title: -webkit-font-smoothing and -webkit-user-select in deck.css (legacy Webkit prefixes)
findings.evidence: slides/src/styles/deck.css:line ~140 area; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -webkit-user-select: none adjacent to user-select: none
findings.rootCause: font-smoothing is non-standard and deprecated (never standardized); user-select is Baseline CSS Widely and does not need -webkit- prefix in modern browsers
findings.proposal: Remove -webkit-font-smoothing entirely (it is a legacy proprietary feature with no standard path). Keep user-select: none; remove -webkit-user-select: none (Firefox and modern Chrome handle user-select without prefix).

findings.title: -webkit-print-color-adjust redundant in print media query
findings.evidence: slides/src/styles/deck.css:@media print rule; body { -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }
findings.rootCause: print-color-adjust is Baseline CSS; -webkit- prefix was needed pre-2021 but is now redundant in all shipping browsers

findings.area: Fragile CSS Rules Audit: glass-ui & slides deck system
findings.summary: Comprehensive read-only analysis of CSS fragility in the slides deck system and glass-ui libraries identified five distinct P-severity findings: (1) viewport-unit traps in edge-zone arrows that scale with 12vw/2vw (brittle on ultra-wide or portrait), (2) cqx-below-floor mobile squish at 390px where all clamp() terms sink to their hard floors, breaking the √φ spacing rhythm, (3) hardcoded grid ratios (1.34fr/0.92fr, 0.78fr/1.7fr) in Slide06/09 that can't reflow smoothly on mobile without manual breakpoints, (4) z-index fragmentation across slides (levels: -1, 0, 1, 2, 4, 40, 45, 50) with no coherent stacking strategy, and (5) aspect-ratio media trap in Slide09's wave-wrap (3/1 portrait breakpoint) that forces manual recalc instead of using intrinsic sizing. All findings include concrete file:line citations and propose idiomatic replacements using container queries, clamp() sane floors, and aspect-ratio constraints.

findings.title: Viewport-Unit Trap in Edge-Zone Navigation Arrows
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/styles/deck.css:788 `width: clamp(64px, 12vw, 160px)` and :792-793 `padding-left: clamp(8px, 2vw, 28px)` / padding-right: clamp(8px, 2vw, 28px)`
findings.rootCause: Edge arrows use `vw` units (viewport width) inside clamp(), violating the deck's cqi-only philosophy. On portrait or extreme aspect ratios, 12vw becomes illogical (e.g., 390px mobile: 12vw = 46.8px, floor binds). On ultra-wide (e.g., 2560px), 12vw = 307px, far exceeding the 160px ceiling—wasteful sizing. The vw term is also unreactive to the 16:9 stage letterbox.
findings.proposal: Replace `clamp(64px, 12vw, 160px)` with `clamp(56px, 8cqi, 80px)` (scales with stage width, binds only at authoring floor/ceiling). Replace `clamp(8px, 2vw, 28px)` with `clamp(6px, 1.5cqi, 14px)`. This ties the arrows to the deck's canonical 1280cqi reference frame and respects the portrait reflow where arrows are hidden (@media pointer:coarse).
findings.gate: proof:deck-edge arrows remain visible on all viewport scales after change; no visual regression on 390px or 2560px

findings.title: Mobile Squish: cqi Terms Below Floor at 390px Break Type Rhythm
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/styles/deck.css:96-104 type-scale tokens with cqi terms (e.g., `--type-prose: clamp(16px, 1.40625cqi, 23px)` and `--type-heading: clamp(22px, 2.0225cqi, 33px)`). Comment at line 96-99 states 'at 390px every cqi term sinks below its floor'.
findings.rootCause: The cqx anchor is `calc(1cqi / 12.8)`, so 1cqi = 100/12.8 ≈ 7.8px at 390px viewport. All type-scale cqi terms resolve below their hard floors: e.g., `1.40625cqi ≈ 11px < 16px floor` on prose, forcing every element to its minimum. This collapses the intended √φ spacing hierarchy (prose ≈ subheading < heading < title < display should feel graduated, not pinned). The deck's comment acknowledges the issue but treats it as 'export-safe'; it is NOT safe for live portrait viewing.
findings.proposal: Introduce a portrait-specific type-scale layer inside `@media (max-aspect-ratio: 1/1)` that overrides the global clamp() tokens with a new √φ ladder pinned to a 390px-aware floor. E.g., `--type-prose-portrait: clamp(14px, 3.5cqi, 20px)` and `--type-heading-portrait: clamp(18px, 5cqi, 28px)`. Apply these via `.slide[data-state='active'] @container (width < 600px)` to preserve the live gradient while respecting mobile's reduced stage width. Alternatively, adopt a two-tier cqx system: `--cqx-landscape: calc(1cqi / 12.8)` and `--cqx-portrait: calc(1cqi / 6.4)` (double the ratio) for portrait, so the same cqi terms never dip below floor.
findings.gate: proof:at 390px portrait, type-display reads >=34px, type-prose >=16px, and spacing hierarchy is felt across all transitions

findings.title: Hardcoded Grid-Column Ratios Lock Slide Layout on Mobile
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/slides/Slide06.vue:156 `.body { grid-template-columns: 1.34fr 0.92fr; }` and /Slide09.vue:163 `.scope { grid-template-columns: 0.78fr 1.7fr; }`. Both declare hardcoded fractional ratios that assume desktop width; mobile @container rules cascade down but reflow entire column (grid-template-columns: 1fr) without intermediate breakpoints.
findings.rootCause: Fractional units (fr) are inflexible at mobile scales. Slide06's 1.34fr/0.92fr ratio assumes 1280px width; at 390px portrait, the left pan (1.34fr) gets 63% and right (0.92fr) gets 37%. The balance-grid inside (1fr / 64px / 1fr) tries to maintain symmetry, but at portrait the 64px central fulcrum becomes a hard pixel sink, cramping the pans. The @container (width < 700px) reflow stacks to 1fr, losing the original proportion intent entirely.
findings.proposal: Replace hardcoded fr ratios with responsive calc() expressions or dynamic grid-auto-fit. For Slide06, use `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.34fr) minmax(0, 0.92fr)` to allow flex shrinking. For portrait, adopt `grid-template-columns: 1fr` ONLY when the computed desktop ratio would invert (i.e., introduce a finer intermediate breakpoint at width < 900px where the ratio softens to 1.1fr / 0.9fr before fully stacking). Alternatively, use CSS Grid's `auto-fit` with `minmax()` to let column count respond: `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(calc(1.34fr * 100%), 350px), 1fr))` so each column shrinks to a sane minimum before wrapping.
findings.gate: proof:Slide06 pans remain visually balanced at all widths >=280px; no content overflow or weird aspect shifts

findings.title: Z-Index Stacking Fragmentation Across Slide Layers
findings.evidence: Multiple files: /deck.css:250 `.slide[data-state='active'] { z-index: 2; }`, :305 `.slide::after { z-index: 0; }`, :311 `.slide > * { z-index: 1; }`, :575 `.deck-dock-wrap { z-index: 50; }`, :667 `.deck-progress { z-index: 40; }`, :787 `.deck-edge { z-index: 45; }`. Slide-local z-indices in Slide08.vue:330 `.seam { z-index: 4; }`, Slide02.vue:89 `.headline .nobody::after { z-index: -1; }`, and Slide10.vue:107, 113, 163, 214 various `.node { z-index: 2; }` declarations.
findings.rootCause: No coherent z-index strategy. The deck.css establishes a global stack (0 = grain, 1 = content, 2 = active slide, 40+ = chrome), but individual slides declare local z-indices (-1, 2, 4) that create sub-contexts within the slide's `isolation: isolate` (deck.css:244). When Slide10 uses z-index: 2 on `.node`, it can collide invisibly with the active slide's z-index: 2 if the scope is not correctly nested. The absolute positioning of pseudo-elements with z-index: -1 (Slide02) is brittle—if the parent gains `transform` or `filter`, the stacking context shifts unpredictably.
findings.proposal: Establish a single root z-index ladder as CSS custom properties in :root or .deck, with named tiers: `--zi-grain: 0, --zi-content: 10, --zi-overlay: 20, --zi-chrome: 100, --zi-modal: 1000`. Replace all local z-indices with these tokens. For slide-local elements, introduce `--zi-slide-accent: 5` and `--zi-slide-overlay: 15` (scoped inside `.slide` so they map to global layers 10+5=15, 10+15=25). Use CSS counters or a Sass mixin to auto-generate the ladder per-slide. Remove all negative z-indices; use `mix-blend-mode` or `opacity` instead to achieve layering without inversion.
findings.gate: proof:no visual regressions in stacking order across all slides in light + dark modes; seams and overlays render in intended depth

findings.title: Manual Aspect-Ratio Breakpoint in Slide09 Wave Container (Avoidable)
findings.evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src/decks/til-briefing/slides/Slide09.vue:299 `.wave-wrap { aspect-ratio: 3 / 1; flex: 0 0 auto; min-height: 0; }` inside @container (width < 700px). Comment at line 298: '3/1 narrows the gap to the SVG's natural 8.33:1 — 5/2 overcrowded the zigzag'.
findings.rootCause: The wave SVG has a viewBox of 0 0 600 72, an intrinsic ratio of 8.33:1. Desktop lets it fit freely inside `.wave-wrap { flex: 1 1 auto; }`. On portrait, the manually-hardcoded 3/1 ratio is a magic number derived from trial-and-error ('5/2 overcrowded'). If the SVG content changes (more cycles in the waveform) or the space budget shifts, the ratio must be manually re-tuned. This violates the deck's cqi-led responsivity—aspect-ratio should scale with the space available, not be a static constant.
findings.proposal: Replace the hardcoded `aspect-ratio: 3/1` with an intrinsic container-query-aware ratio: use `aspect-ratio: auto / 3` (or a CSS variable `--wave-ratio: 3`) that reads from a data attribute or computed style. Better: adopt `aspect-ratio: attr(data-aspect-ratio 16 / 9)` on the SVG itself, defaulting to the viewBox ratio, so no slide CSS is needed. For portrait, apply `aspect-ratio: 100% / 40%` (auto-computed from container height) instead of a magic 3/1. Or: use a CSS anchor positioning or computed `clamp(2, var(--space-available) / 600px * 8.33, 4)` to derive the ratio dynamically from available space.
findings.gate: proof:wave-wrap maintains readable waveform at all mobile widths; no wiggle in aspect under theme/locale changes

risks: Changing cqx floor strategy (F-002) requires careful auditing of ALL slide-local type-scale overrides to ensure no new collisions arise at portrait breakpoints.
Z-index refactor (F-004) is high-touch: every slide using local z-indices must be retested for stacking regressions, especially where pseudo-elements or nested transforms are involved.
Grid-ratio replacement (F-003) could shift visual balance on intermediate viewports (768-900px tablet range) if not carefully interpolated; recommend testing 5+ explicit breakpoint widths.
Viewport-unit replacement (F-001) in edge arrows is safe but requires double-check that the cqi scale is correct in both landscape (desktop) and portrait (mobile) orientations.

findings.area: Design-idiom localization and Tailwind v4 idiom alignment across glass-ui and slides repos
findings.summary: Glass-UI has a well-structured design-idiom area across src/styles/ with tokens.css (custom properties), theme.css (@theme block for Tailwind v4 registration), and utilities.css (@utility recipes), enabling proper colocation: components reference design tokens via scoped <style> blocks without duplicating pattern definitions. Slides lacks this structure entirely—deck.css contains 828 lines of raw CSS with 126 :root custom properties and ZERO @theme/@utility blocks, forcing design identity invisible to Tailwind and scattered across semantic classes (.card, .chip, .eyebrow). The documented F.W6 wave (slides) proposes extracting deck-theme.css as a new localized idiom area with @theme (color/motion/shadow Tailwind registration) and @utility recipes (card/chip/typography bundles), keeping deck.css layout-only. GU's pattern is the canonical target: design tokens → @theme registration → Tailwind utility composition, all colocated in src/styles/, with components consuming via scoped CSS variable references (no class duplication).

findings.title: Glass-UI has canonical design-idiom localization: tokens.css → theme.css → utilities.css → component scoped CSS
findings.evidence: GU/src/styles/index.css:38-51 documents cascade order: (1) tokens.css (CSS custom properties, source-of-record), (2) typography.css, (3) theme.css (@theme block mapping tokens to Tailwind v4 utilities), (4-11) component layers (glass.css, paper.css, dock.css, etc.), (12-17) per-package CSS files. Components reference via scoped <style> blocks: GU/src/components/custom/timeline/ScrubberTimeline.vue uses var(--duration-fast), var(--ease-standard), var(--type-small) — no class duplication, pure token references.
findings.rootCause: Well-factored cascade with clear separation: tokens declare design language, @theme exposes to Tailwind, @utility bundles multi-property recipes, component scopes consume both.
findings.proposal: This is the GOLD STANDARD. GU proves the pattern works: (1) src/styles/tokens.css: CSS custom properties only, zero Tailwind coupling; (2) src/styles/theme.css: @theme block aliasing all public tokens to Tailwind utility names; (3) src/styles/utilities.css/@layer components: @utility recipes for multi-property bundles (popover-animate, slide-in-from-side, labeled-field-label, labeled-field error states); (4) component <style scoped>: consume ONLY CSS custom properties and @utility classes, never raw theme aliases; (5) index.css: single @source ../components line ensures Tailwind scans component templates for utility usage. Idiomatic Tailwind v4 colocation.

findings.title: Slides deck.css is a 828-line monolith mixing layout, tokens, and semantic classes with ZERO @theme/@utility blocks
findings.evidence: SL/src/styles/deck.css:1-136 has §1 (TOKENS): 126 :root custom properties (--ncsu-red, --red-wash, --ai-blue-*, --shadow-cartoon-lg, --ease-out, --spring-deck, --shadow-soft/md/lg/xl, --cqx, --deck-dock-clearance); §2-10 (LAYOUT/BEHAVIOR): .deck, .slide, [data-reveal], @keyframes rise/fade/wipe-x/grow-y/deck-gate-shake, pager, dock chrome, export/print modes; §3 (TYPOGRAPHY): .text-display-2/.text-title/.text-heading/etc. (multi-property bundles); §4 (SURFACES): .card, .card--cartoon, .card--flag; §5 (COMPONENTS): .chip, .badge, .steps. Zero @theme block, zero @utility recipes. Contrast GU/src/styles/index.css:95-113 which imports tokens.css separately, then theme.css, then component utilities (glass.css, paper.css, etc.).
findings.rootCause: Slides was built pre-Tailwind-v4 idiom. deck.css evolved as a monolithic garden-shed CSS file. No refactoring to expose identity via @theme/@utility, no colocation strategy.
findings.proposal: Create NEW SL/src/styles/deck-theme.css as the canonical localized design-idiom area (following F.W6 audit L13): (1) @theme block (G1/L13:144-176) registering deck color/motion/shadow as Tailwind utilities: --color-ncsu-red, --color-red-text, --color-ai-blue-*, --ease-deck-out, --ease-deck-standard, --spring-deck-page, --shadow-deck-stamp (rename from --shadow-cartoon-lg to avoid GU collision, F2/L13:33-59). (2) @utility recipes for multi-property bundles (G2/L13:190-248): @utility card, @utility card-cartoon, @utility card-flag, @utility chip, @utility chip-red, @utility badge; and (G3/L13:255-267) @utility for typography (.text-display-2, .text-title, .text-heading, .eyebrow, .section-label, .mono). Rename deck.css §1 --shadow-cartoon-lg to --shadow-deck-stamp (slides-only fix, no GU change). Update all 11 slide templates + HomeView/NotFound to use utility names instead of class names (mechanical BEM-to-utility rename: .card--cartoon → card-cartoon). deck.css retains §2-10 (layout/geometry/behavior), becomes layout-only. Index.css imports order: @import 'tailwindcss'; @import 'tw-animate-css'; @import '@mkbabb/glass-ui/styles'; @import './deck-theme.css'; @import './deck.css'; @variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)); @source. This mirrors GU's pattern exactly.

findings.title: Slides deck.css has latent token-namespace clobber: --shadow-cartoon-lg/--shadow-md/lg/xl override GU's @theme chains
findings.evidence: SL/src/styles/deck.css:116-121 declares --shadow-cartoon-lg: 7px 7px 0 0 ..., --shadow-md: 0 8px 28px ..., --shadow-lg: 0 18px 48px ..., --shadow-xl: 0 30px 70px ... (deeper cartoon shadows, deliberate per comment 'kept as deck identity'). GU/src/styles/tokens.css + theme.css map --shadow-cartoon-lg, --shadow-soft/md/lg to @theme entries via var() chains (not literals), so deck.css :root overrides intercept the Tailwind utilities. Per L13/F2:33-59, zero render impact TODAY (no GU components use shadow-cartoon-lg as a Tailwind utility class), but a latent trap: future GU component using shadow-cartoon-lg class would get deck's flat stamp, not GU's angled drop.
findings.rootCause: deck.css uses generic GU token names (--shadow-cartoon-lg) for deck-specific values, creating silent namespace collision via CSS cascade.
findings.proposal: Rename deck.css --shadow-cartoon-lg → --shadow-deck-stamp-lg, --shadow-cartoon-red → --shadow-deck-stamp-red (slides-only, no GU change per L13/G4:271-278). Update all references in deck.css §4 (.card--cartoon shadow prop) to use new names. This isolates deck identity from GU's namespace and eliminates the latent trap. Isomorphic: render identical today; future-safe. Per L13 pre-ship gate (L17-19): grep -rEn '\.card\s+\.|chip\s+\.' src/decks/ MUST = 0 before shipping (specificity precondition for @utility layer lower than global class rules).

findings.title: Slides typography semantic classes (.text-display-2/.eyebrow/etc.) shadow GU's @theme --text-* utilities with zero documentation
findings.evidence: SL/src/styles/deck.css:340-368 defines .text-display-2, .text-title, .text-heading, .eyebrow, .section-label as full multi-property bundles (font-family + font-size + line-height + font-weight + letter-spacing). GU/src/styles/theme.css registers @theme { --text-prose, --text-title, etc. }, generating Tailwind utilities. deck.css's .text-* classes have higher specificity (they are global class rules, not utility layer), so they mask Tailwind's font-size-only utilities. Per L13/F5:99-117, this is INTENTIONAL (deck type is always a full bundle, not a utility composition), but invisible to future template authors who might compose text-prose text-[color] expecting Tailwind composability.
findings.rootCause: Intentional shadowing with zero documentation. A one-line comment explaining the intentional precedence would suffice (per L13/F5 recommendation).
findings.proposal: Add comment at SL/src/styles/deck.css §3 top (before .text-display-2): '/* INTENTIONAL SHADOWING: these semantic classes (.text-display-2, .eyebrow, etc.) intentionally shadow GU's @theme --text-* font-size utilities. Deck typography is always set as a full-bundle rule (font-family + size + line-height + weight), not a composable Tailwind utility. See L13/F5 for rationale. */' Alternatively, in the G3 refactor (SL-1), convert these to @utility recipes with explicit multi-property bundling, formally documenting the intentional design. Zero render delta.

findings.title: Canonical design-idiom localization pattern: colocation = tokens + @theme + @utility + scoped component styles, all in src/styles/
findings.evidence: GU/src/styles/index.css:38-51 (cascade order with rationale); GU/src/styles/tokens.css:1-11 (custom properties, source-of-record); GU/src/styles/theme.css:1-8 (@theme block mapping); GU/src/styles/utilities.css:1-12, 26-37 (@utility popover-animate, slide-in-from-side, section-description, labeled-field-label); GU/src/components/custom/timeline/ScrubberTimeline.vue:<style> (scoped uses var(--duration-fast), var(--type-small), var(--radius-sm) — pure token references, no class name duplication). SL/src/styles/deck.css:1-136 violates this: 828 lines mixing tokens + layout + semantic classes, no @theme/@utility, no colocation.
findings.rootCause: GU chose gestalt design-system architecture; slides evolved as project-specific monolith. No architectural parity.
findings.proposal: Canonical single-source-of-truth for BOTH repos: src/styles/{tokens.css, theme.css, utilities.css} contain ALL design idiom declarations (color, motion, shadow, typography bundles, surface recipes). Components declare: (1) template: use HTML + Tailwind utility classes + glass-ui @utility classes (popover-animate, slide-in-from-side, card, chip, etc.); (2) <style scoped>: consume ONLY CSS custom properties (var(--*)) + @utility classes, never hardcoded color/motion/shadow literals. No per-component CSS duplication of design tokens. Index.css @import order: tokens.css → typography.css → theme.css → {glass/paper/dock/...}.css → utilities.css → per-package component CSS. @source ../components ensures Tailwind scans templates. For slides: apply GU's pattern via deck-theme.css (L13/T1). For GU: already canonical; document in CLAUDE.md / DESIGN.md as the reference architecture for consumers.

findings.title: Glass-UI @utility recipes (popover-animate, slide-in-from-side, labeled-field-label) enable multi-property bundling without class-name duplication
findings.evidence: GU/src/styles/utilities.css:8-24 (@utility popover-animate, @utility slide-in-from-side using @apply data-[state=...] patterns); utilities.css:32-37 (@utility section-description: font-size + color + line-height); utilities.css:45-68 (.labeled-field + .labeled-field:has(:user-invalid) + .labeled-field-error for reactive state bundling). These are declared once in the library's canonical utilities layer, not scattered in component scopes. Any component using popover-animate class gets consistent animation state binding.
findings.rootCause: Intentional design: @utility form registers multi-property recipes at the library level so components consume via class names, not via scoped CSS duplication.
findings.proposal: This pattern is BEST PRACTICE. Slides should adopt it (SL-1). GU should continue extending it: any multi-property bundle that appears in ≥2 components becomes an @utility candidate. Examples already exemplify: card (5-rung glass ladder surface bundles), chip (inline-flex + gap + padding + border + font), typography (font-family + size + line-height + weight). GU's precept: '@utility lifts require ≥2 real consumers (storybook demo does NOT count)' — this prevents bloat while keeping the library lean.

findings.title: Slides deck.css has redundant @keyframes deck-gate-shake (mirrors GU's @keyframes shake)
findings.evidence: SL/src/styles/deck.css:708-713 (@keyframes deck-gate-shake oscillating translateX); GU/src/styles/animations.css has @keyframes shake with nearly identical logic. Per L13/F4:79-95, both animate ±2px translateX, differ by 1–2px. deck-gate-shake is a local duplicate that could reference GU's shake directly.
findings.rootCause: Pre-Tailwind refactoring: deck-gate-shake was authored locally before identifying the shared pattern.
findings.proposal: Minor deduplication per L13/R5: replace .deck-gate__form--shake { animation: deck-gate-shake 0.42s ease; } with animation: shake 0.42s ease; (reuse GU's @keyframes). Zero render delta. Low priority (R5 maps to minor improvement, not gate-blocking).

risks: Slides deck.css :root --shadow-cartoon-lg override is invisible until a future GU component uses shadow-cartoon-lg as a Tailwind utility class in the deck context—then render divergence surfaces. Mitigation: rename to --shadow-deck-stamp-lg (SL-2) and document in deck-theme.css.

Converting slides semantic classes (.card, .chip, .eyebrow) to @utility recipes (SL-1/G2) is atomic and mechanical (BEM -- to utility - naming), but MUST be coordinated across all 11 slides + HomeView + NotFound + DeckSettings in a single commit. No partial migrations. Specificity precondition: grep -rEn '\.card\s+\.|\chip\s+\.' src/decks/ = 0 (no scoped descendant selectors that would fight @utility layer lower specificity). Gate before shipping.

GU's component-scoping strategy (scoped <style> consuming var(--*) only) is undocumented in DESIGN.md/CLAUDE.md. If the pattern is aspirational rather than current-state enforced, some components may hardcode color/shadow/easing values outside the token system. Audit required: grep -r 'rgb\|hsl\|cubic-bezier\|[0-9]ms\|[0-9]s' src/components/custom --include='*.vue' | grep -v node_modules to find hardcoded literals in scoped styles. Any hits = colocation violation.

Slides has NO TypeScript token definitions (GU has src/tokens.ts exporting CSS custom property names as constants). Slide templates use raw CSS strings (var(--ncsu-red)). If deck-theme.css is created, TypeScript types should follow (export enum Colors { NCSU_RED = '--color-ncsu-red', ... }) so template authors can import token names rather than stringifying them.

GU's @utility layer (utilities.css, transitions.css, animations.css, per-package CSS) is documented by CASCADE ORDER in index.css:38-51, but no DESIGN.md section explains the @utility/component-colocation contract for NEW contributions. Document explicitly: '@utility candidates: multi-property bundles used in ≥2 components; component-scoped <style>: consume ONLY CSS custom properties + @utility classes, never hardcoded literals.'

findings.area: Slides Deck til-briefing: CSS Selectors, Reactivity, and Design Cohesion Audit
findings.summary: The til-briefing deck exhibits strong cohesion around glass-ui's warm-cream glassmorphism + Fraunces + NCSU-red aesthetic with no major combinator typos detected. Reactivity binds cleanly via `[data-state="active"]` on the `.slide` container (deck.css), avoiding brittle descendant chains. All 11 slides composably use the deck's token system (colors, shadows, radiuses via CSS custom properties), adopt cartoon offset shadows, and maintain the cqi-fluid golden-ratio type scale. Minor concerns: two-tier selector nesting in slides (e.g., `.presenter__people span`, `.snap .frozen`) presents mild brittleness if DOM structure shifts; zero :deep() or >>> violations found; animation timing chains lean on JavaScript readiness (nextTick) which is safe. No isomorphic style divergence detected—design is idiomatically glass-ui throughout.

findings.title: Slide07 bar + arc animations bind safely to active state
findings.evidence: Slide07.vue:193–195 (`[data-state="active"] .bar__rail`, `[data-state="active"] .bar--then .bar__rail`, `[data-state="active"] .bar--now .bar__rail`) and line 231 (`[data-state="active"] .arc-fill`). Selectors correctly use attribute selector on scoped .slide root, no space typos, no stray IDs. animations trigger only when parent slide is active.
findings.rootCause: Alleged combinator typo (`.slide.is-active #slide-07 .bar__rail` with stray space) does NOT exist in codebase. Current selectors are properly scoped and functional.
findings.proposal: No fix required. The claimed typo audit finding is a false alarm—the deck does not use ID-based slide targeting, relying instead on declarative `[data-state]` binding and scoped styles. This is the correct pattern.

findings.title: Reactivity architecture avoids brittle DOM selectors
findings.evidence: deck.css:533–540 defines animation triggers on `.slide[data-state="active"] [data-reveal]` and `.slide[data-state="active"] [data-reveal="fade"]`. useDeckNav.ts:56–58 queries only the active slide once for countup settlement. No querySelector loops scanning slide indices or relying on sibling DOM order.
findings.rootCause: Architecture is sound: Vue reactivity (via [data-state] binding in DeckView) drives visibility; CSS and JS both read the same signal. Slides are interchangeable; reordering never breaks reactivity.
findings.proposal: No changes needed. The current pattern (attribute-based state binding + declarative CSS) is robust and idiomatic. Maintain this for future slides.

findings.title: Two-tier descendant selectors present mild coupling to DOM structure
findings.evidence: Slide01.vue:182 (`.presenter__people span`), Slide03.vue:212–213 (`.glyph .stroke`, `.glyph .faint`), Slide07.vue:138 (`.head .stack`), Slide09.vue:195 (`.snap .frozen`), Slide10.vue:256 (`.signoff__people span`). All are scoped, but a refactor shifting intermediates (e.g., wrapping `.presenter__people span` in a div) would break styling.
findings.rootCause: Descendant combinators (` ` space) are tighter than child combinators (`>`) and bind to any nested element, not just direct children. No alternate tree structure anticipated in slide authoring—risk is low but real.
findings.proposal: Adopt child combinators (`>`) in new slides where the DOM depth is stable. Backport safe cases: `.presenter__people > span` (Slide01:182), `.snap > .frozen` (only if .frozen is a direct child—verify structure). No urgent refactor needed, but document in slide authoring guide: "Use child combinator (>) for element groups with stable depth."

findings.title: Design cohesion is strong; glass-ui tokens consistently applied
findings.evidence: All 11 slides compose `.card`, `.card--cartoon`, `.card--flag` (deck.css:408–434), use `var(--ncsu-red)`, `var(--ncsu-red-bright)`, `var(--ncsu-red-ink)`, `var(--red-wash)`, `var(--red-text)`, and cartoon offset shadows (e.g., Slide01:165 `background: var(--ncsu-red)`, Slide08:295 `box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 0 var(--ai-blue-shadow)`). No raw hex colors or bespoke shadows; all type uses the cqi-fluid ladder (--type-display-2, --type-title, --type-prose, etc.). Fraunces display font and letterforms match glass-ui's signature.
findings.rootCause: Slides systematically reference deck tokens (§1 of deck.css). There is no style drift: red/cream/ink/glass registers are honored. The --ai-blue register (Slide08 AI/human loop) is a single-consumer token defined at deck root (deck.css:40–50), properly scoped.
findings.proposal: No changes. The design is isomorphic to glass-ui's aesthetic. Continue this pattern for new slides. Document: "Every color, shadow, radius, and type size is a CSS custom property—no pasted values."

findings.title: Entrance reveal choreography depends on nextTick timing, not DOM order
findings.evidence: useDeckNav.ts:49–51 calls `runActiveCountups()` via nextTick after Vue reflects new `[data-state]`. Countup elements (data-countup) are queried globally (line 83: `document.querySelectorAll`), not by slide. v-reveal stagger (deck.css:538) uses CSS delay calculated from `var(--d, 0)`, a per-element attribute.
findings.rootCause: Reveal timing is brittle if the active slide DOM is still rendering when JS runs the countup query. nextTick ensures Vue has flushed updates, but if a countup or reveal element is mounted asynchronously (unlikely in this codebase), the timing could slip.
findings.proposal: Very low risk: the deck's reveal grammar (all [data-reveal] attributes are static in templates). No v-if branching hides/shows reveal elements per slide; reveals are always DOM-present. Confirm this invariant in an architectural doc. No code changes needed now.

findings.title: Glass highlight and cartoon shadows compose idiomatically without conflict
findings.evidence: deck.css:414–415 pairs `box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg), var(--glass-highlight)` on `.card`, and `.card--cartoon` (420) uses `box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-lg), var(--glass-highlight)`. Slides follow: Slide03:193 (`.tile:hover { box-shadow: var(--shadow-xl), var(--glass-highlight) }`), Slide09:261 (same pattern). The glass-highlight inset halo is always second, preserving depth.
findings.rootCause: Shadow composition is correct: CSS multiple box-shadows layer front-to-back in declaration order. Inset halo (glass-highlight, defined deck.css:80) sits on top, creating the signature glass gleam.
findings.proposal: No changes. Maintain this pattern in all new cards. Document: "Always compose shadows as: [depth shadow], [glass-highlight] for consistent glass-ui aesthetic."

findings.title: Slide--dark forced dark mode is properly isolated; no color-scheme leakage
findings.evidence: Slide04 and Slide11 are dark feature slides (visible in `<section class="slide" data-slide="4">` and `class="slide" data-slide="11">`—both force `.slide--dark` via data attributes). deck.css:315–332 redefines color tokens when .slide--dark is active. No slides mix light and dark within the same section.
findings.rootCause: Architecture isolates dark slides: each slide is a color-scheme boundary. Constellation opacity and anomaly accent are also adjusted (deck.css:891 dark mode lift). No subcomponent risks conflicting color-scheme values.
findings.proposal: No changes. The forced-dark pattern is idiomatic and safe. Confirm in authoring docs: "Dark feature slides set .slide--dark; deck tokens automatically resolve to the dark arm."

findings.title: Portrait reflows use @container queries correctly; no stray media queries
findings.evidence: All 11 slides use `@container (width < 700px)` blocks (e.g., Slide01:186, Slide08:390, Slide11:213). The .deck is the container root (deck.css:171 `container-type: inline-size`). No bare @media queries in slide styles that would operate at the viewport level (which would ignore the 1280cqi export-mode override).
findings.rootCause: Container queries are the correct primitive for scoped responsive design. Queries on slide width, not viewport width, ensure export mode (1280px forced deck) doesn't reflow slides.
findings.proposal: No changes. This is best practice. Maintain @container for all responsive rules in new slides; forbid @media in scoped styles.

findings.title: color-mix() usage is consistent and accessible; no legacy rgba fallbacks
findings.evidence: Slides consistently use `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ncsu-red) 45%, transparent)` (e.g., Slide04:173, Slide07:151). No mixed rgba/color-mix in the same codebase. deck.css also uses color-mix exclusively (lines 31–32, 116–121, etc.).
findings.rootCause: color-mix is modern and uniform across the deck. The srgb color space is explicit, matching deck intent. No cross-browser fallback needed (Safari 16+, Chrome 111+, all modern targets).
findings.proposal: No changes. Maintain color-mix consistently. No legacy rgba needed.
